chapters.chapter_summary:
Sunny, a poor and frail young man living in the outskirts of a dystopian world, realizes he has been infected by the Nightmare Spell after experiencing extreme sleepiness for a week. Knowing he is likely to die, he spends most of his savings on real coffee before surrendering himself to the police.

 The Nightmare Spell first appeared decades ago, causing people to fall into unnatural sleep and transform into monsters upon death. Those who survive its trials become Awakened, gaining extraordinary abilities. However, Sunny has little chance of survival because he lacks the resources, training, and family support available to wealthier people.

 At the police station, Sunny is restrained in a heavily fortified room. An experienced policeman explains that his First Nightmare will test his ability to survive and that he must examine his Attributes and Aspect upon entering.

If Sunny dies, a Nightmare Creature will emerge into the real world. As exhaustion finally overwhelms him, Sunny falls asleep and hears the Spell announce the beginning of his First Trial.
chapters.chapter_summary_condensed:
Sunny surrenders himself to the police after becoming a carrier of the Nightmare Spell.

He is taken into custody and prepared to enter his First Nightmare.

 An older policeman explains some basic information about the Nightmare Spell and its effects. Sunny enters the Nightmare and is now an Aspirant.

chapters.chapter_summary:
Sunny dreams of a mysterious mountain where he witnesses time moving backward before suddenly returning to normal. He then finds himself in a terrifying situation: he is a weak, starving slave chained to a long line of other prisoners as they travel through a freezing mountain pass. Sunny is confused because this is his First Nightmare Trial, and he expected to have a better chance of surviving. Instead, he is cold, injured, and surrounded by danger. Sunny discovers how to view his status through magical runes, hoping to find a powerful ability that will help him survive. However, he is shocked to learn that his Aspect is [Temple Slave], which is described as practically useless. He also discovers three mysterious attributes: [Fated], [Mark of Divinity], and [Child of Shadows]. Despite his terrible starting position, Sunny believes the Nightmare Spell should provide some balance to the challenge, so he hopes that his other attributes might give him an advantage. As the caravan continues, Sunny interacts with two other slaves: a broad-shouldered man who has little hope of surviving the mountain and a nervous, quick-tempered man who constantly insults Sunny. A third slave explains that Sunny was born into slavery because he was a temple slave, connected to the Shadow God, whose last temple was recently destroyed by the Empire. Meanwhile, a young soldier takes pity on Sunny and offers him water, but an older, cruel soldier intervenes and whips Sunny for disrupting the caravan. The older soldier insists that slaves should not be treated like people, and he threatens the younger soldier for showing kindness.

By the end of the chapter, Sunny becomes filled with anger and a desire for revenge. Although he is physically weak and seems to have an almost worthless Aspect, his determination to survive remains strong. He silently promises himself that he will eventually see both soldiers die, showing that beneath his helpless appearance lies a stubborn and potentially dangerous personality.
chapters.chapter_summary_condensed: Sunny enters his First Nightmare and finds himself as a young slave being forced to travel up a cold mountain pass. He is shackled to a long chain alongside dozens of other slaves. Sunny discovers his Nightmare status and sees his Aspect and Attributes. His Aspect is [Temple Slave], which appears to provide no useful skills or abilities. Sunny learns that he was born a slave and is specifically a temple slave associated with the Shadow God. The slaves are being transported by soldiers of the Empire. A young soldier attempts to give Sunny water, but an older soldier stops him and punishes Sunny instead. Sunny develops hostility toward both soldiers.

chapters.chapter_summary:
Sunny regains his composure and accepts his situation, knowing that his First Nightmare is likely to end in a deadly monster attack. He examines his Attributes and realizes that [Fated] attracts unlikely events, both good and bad, while [Mark of Divinity] seems mostly useless in his current circumstances. However, [Child of Shadows] grants him the ability to see perfectly in darkness, giving him a potential advantage.

As night approaches, the caravan stops to camp. The exhausted slaves huddle around a bonfire but receive barely enough food and water to satisfy their hunger. Sunny observes the other slaves, including a shifty man who nearly eats poisonous Bloodbane berries before a scholarly-looking slave warns him of their danger.

Sunny then recognizes the campsite from his earlier vision, where he saw the remains of dead slaves buried beneath the snow. Realizing that the deadly event is about to happen, he prepares for the worst. Suddenly, a thunderous noise echoes from above, and something enormous comes crashing down from the sky.
chapters.chapter_summary_condensed: Sunny continues traveling with the slave caravan up the mountain. Several slaves become unable to continue and are thrown from the mountain. Sunny realizes that the caravan is approaching the location where he previously saw the bones of the slaves in his vision. He expects the caravan to be attacked within hours. Sunny examines his Attributes more carefully and learns what they do. His [Child of Shadows] Attribute allows him to see perfectly in darkness. The caravan stops to camp for the night. Sunny receives a small amount of water and food. He meets the gentle-voiced slave, a scholar-like man in his forties. The scholar explains that the red berries growing along the road are poisonous Bloodbane. The camp is established at the same location Sunny saw in his earlier vision. Something massive suddenly crashes down from above.

chapters.chapter_summary:
Rocks and chunks of ice begin raining down on the caravan, causing panic among the slaves. Sunny stays alert and avoids the falling debris, but a massive monster soon crashes onto the campsite. The towering creature has five white eyes, thick fur, bone claws, and strange movements beneath its skin. It attacks the slaves, killing the broad-shouldered man beside Sunny.

Trapped beneath the man's corpse, Sunny struggles to free himself. He discovers that the dead slave's body is transforming into another monster, an ability normally associated with powerful Nightmare Creatures called Tyrants. Realizing that his First Nightmare contains a creature far stronger than expected, Sunny understands that his [Fated] Attribute may be responsible for this terrible situation.

With little time to react, Sunny uses his street survival instincts to wrap the chain around the transforming creature and immobilize its arms. He orders the shifty slave and the scholarly slave to pull the chain tight, then uses the chain connecting his own shackles to restrain the monster's neck. Despite his injuries and limited strength, Sunny struggles with all his might until the creature finally goes limp. The Spell announces that he has slain a dormant beast called the Mountain King's Larva.
chapters.chapter_summary_condensed: The slave caravan is attacked by falling rocks and ice. A huge Nightmare Creature appears and begins attacking the slaves. Sunny avoids the creature's first attack by using the broad-shouldered slave as a shield. The broad-shouldered slave is killed, and his corpse begins transforming into another creature. Sunny realizes that the transformed creature is far stronger than what should normally appear in a First Nightmare. Sunny uses the caravan's chain to restrain the transformed creature. With help from the shifty slave and the scholarly slave, Sunny uses his shackles and body weight to strangle the creature. Sunny successfully kills it. The Spell identifies the creature as a Mountain King's Larva and a Dormant Beast.

chapters.chapter_summary:
After killing the Mountain King's Larva, Sunny is left exhausted but exhilarated. However, the Nightmare is far from over, as several more corpses begin transforming into larvae while the Mountain King continues slaughtering the remaining slaves and soldiers. Just as another larva attacks Sunny and his two companions, the young soldier who previously showed Sunny kindness appears and kills it with a single sword strike. Before rushing off to fight the remaining monsters, he throws Sunny a key to unlock his shackles.

Sunny frees himself and then unlocks the shifty slave and the scholarly slave. While Shifty wants to flee, Scholar warns that leaving the bonfire would mean freezing to death in the surrounding mountains. Sunny agrees that staying near the fire offers their best chance, but he doubts the soldiers can defeat the Mountain King, a powerful Tyrant. Determined to survive, Sunny decides to approach the ongoing battle and find a way to deal with the monster himself, despite Shifty's disbelief at his apparent recklessness.
chapters.chapter_summary_condensed: Sunny recovers after killing the Mountain King's Larva. He discovers that several other corpses have transformed into additional larvae. Four new larvae appear and attack the remaining slaves. The young soldier who previously offered Sunny water arrives and kills one of the larvae with a single sword strike. The young soldier gives Sunny a key that unlocks his shackles before fighting the remaining larvae. Sunny frees himself, then frees the shifty slave and the scholarly slave. The three slaves realize that they cannot simply flee because the bonfire is their only protection from the extreme cold. Sunny decides that their best chance of survival is to confront the Mountain King rather than remain at the campsite. Sunny heads toward the ongoing battle.

chapters.chapter_summary:
Sunny studies the Mountain King and realizes that fighting the powerful Tyrant directly is impossible. As the young soldier continues distracting the creature, Sunny comes up with a plan to use gravity to drag it off the cliff with the heavy wagon. He instructs Shifty and Scholar to remove the wooden wedges holding the wagon in place, while he finds the broken caravan chain and uses a key to attach a loop of shackles to it.

Sunny throws the chain toward the monster, intending to trap its ankle, but the loop unexpectedly catches around its neck instead. Although the trap succeeds, the wagon moves too slowly, and the Mountain King begins trying to break free. The young soldier knocks the creature off balance, buying Sunny and the others precious time to push the wagon toward the cliff. With the Tyrant nearly freeing itself, the outcome depends on whether they can send the wagon over the edge before it escapes.
chapters.chapter_summary_condensed: Sunny approaches the Mountain King, a Tyrant, despite having almost no chance of defeating it directly. Most of the slaves and soldiers have already been killed. Sunny realizes that he cannot defeat the Mountain King through strength or combat. The young soldier continues fighting the Mountain King and serves as a distraction. Sunny develops a plan to use the heavy cargo wagon and the nearby cliff to kill the Mountain King. Sunny finds the broken end of the chain attached to the wagon and connects it to a set of shackles, creating a makeshift loop. He throws the chain toward the Mountain King, intending to trap one of its legs. The plan goes wrong, but the loop accidentally lands around the Mountain King's neck. Shifty and Scholar remove the wedges holding the wagon in place and begin pushing it toward the cliff. The young soldier attacks the Mountain King again, preventing it from immediately breaking free. The wagon is moving toward the cliff, but too slowly. The Mountain King manages to grab the chain around its neck.

chapters.chapter_title: Chapter 7: Three Slaves and a Hero
chapters.chapter_summary:
Sunny and the other two slaves push the wagon toward the cliff until it finally tips over the edge, dragging the Mountain King down with it. Although Sunny hopes the Nightmare is over, his trial continues, and the surviving young soldier, Shifty, and Scholar gather around the bonfire to recover. Nearly everyone else in the caravan has been killed. As they discuss their next move, Sunny remains distant, reflecting on his lifelong difficulty connecting with others and his preference for relying on himself.

The young soldier, Hero, proposes waiting until sunrise before collecting supplies and descending the mountain, promising to let the slaves go free afterward. However, Sunny objects, surprising everyone. When Hero asks him to explain, Sunny reveals that the Mountain King is not dead.
chapters.chapter_summary_condensed: Sunny, Shifty, and Scholar push the cargo wagon toward the cliff while Mountain King struggles against the chain around its neck. The wagon reaches the cliff edge, and Sunny pushes it over. The wagon pulls Mountain King over the cliff, apparently defeating the Tyrant. Sunny expects the First Nightmare to end, but no victory announcement occurs. Hero survives and tells the three slaves to warm themselves by the bonfire. Hero proposes returning down the mountain after sunrise because the wagon's supplies were lost. Sunny rejects the plan, stating that Mountain King is not dead.

chapters.chapter_summary: Sunny convinces Hero, Scholar, and Shifty that the Mountain King survived its fall, arguing that a creature capable of leaping from such a height would not be killed by falling off the cliff. Realizing the monster could return, they gather supplies through the night and prepare to leave at dawn. While searching the dead soldiers, Sunny finds the dying veteran who once mistreated him. He grants the man’s apparent wish for his broken sword and ends his suffering, discovering that killing a human earns the Spell’s recognition. He receives his first Memory, the Silver Bell, whose only described enchantment is that its ringing can be heard from miles away. Sunny also takes the veteran’s warm cloak and boots, while noticing that Shifty is stealing valuables instead of finding clothes
chapters.chapter_summary_condensed: Sunny explains that Mountain King survived the fall because the creature had previously survived a much greater fall without injury. Hero agrees that returning down the mountain would be dangerous and decides the survivors must cross the mountain pass instead. The survivors gather food, water, clothing, and firewood before leaving. Sunny finds the dying older soldier who had previously whipped him. Sunny kills the soldier and receives his first Memory, Silver Bell. Sunny takes the soldier's warm cloak and boots. The four survivors remain awake through the night, fearing Mountain King's return. At dawn, they gather their supplies and leave the campsite.

chapters.chapter_summary: The group discovers that a rockfall has destroyed the road to the mountain pass. Scholar remembers an older pilgrim path higher up the slope, so they begin a dangerous climb, carrying their remaining supplies. As Sunny struggles onward, he reflects on the rewards of completing his First Nightmare: access to Soul Cores, entry into the Dream Realm, an Aspect Ability and its accompanying Flaw, and the possibility of an Aspect evolution or a True Name. The climb is exhausting, and night approaches before they can reach safety.
chapters.chapter_summary_condensed: The survivors discover that the road to the mountain pass has been destroyed by a massive rockfall. Shifty suggests leaving Sunny behind because he is weak and believes Sunny may be cursed. Hero refuses to abandon Sunny. Scholar explains that an older pilgrim path may still lead upward to an undamaged section of the road. The group begins climbing the mountain slope. Sunny leaves his short sword behind to reduce his weight. During the difficult climb, Sunny thinks about what he may receive for completing the First Nightmare. The chapter explains the major benefits and consequences associated with completing the First Nightmare. Night approaches while the group continues climbing.

chapters.chapter_summary: The survivors camp in a sheltered alcove, but Shifty and Scholar grow alarmingly ill from the climb. While keeping watch, Sunny spots the Mountain King returning to the platform below to feed on the dead. When a falling rock draws its attention, the creature looks toward him but does not react further, leading Sunny to realize that it is blind and likely hunts by sound. At dawn, they hurry onward, fearing the monster will come after them once it finishes feeding. Shifty’s condition worsens, and despite Hero taking some of his load, he loses his footing on the icy slope and falls to his death, leaving the remaining three to continue without him.

Sunny, Hero, and Scholar stand over the broken body of Shifty in uneasy silence. Scholar remarks that it was fortunate Hero had already taken most of Shifty's supplies, then quickly covers the coldness of the comment with a show of mourning. Sunny, who has distrusted Scholar from the start because people who are kind for no reason are either fools or monsters, doesn't believe the act for a second. Despite his own unexpected twinge of guilt, he follows the other two as they continue climbing.

The altitude wears them down. The air is thin, the wind is brutal, and the cold seeps through their furs. After hours of struggle, they finally find the old pilgrim path Scholar had described, a narrow road cut from black rock. When Sunny looks back, he notices that Shifty's body has vanished from the rocks below, leaving only bloodstains. The three conclude that Mountain King is following them, either because it knows where they are headed or because it is tracking the scent of blood.

Scholar then offers a solution: make Sunny bleed, drag him down the path, and leave him as bait while the others go up. Sunny had been expecting exactly this and recalls Scholar's earlier remark that the boy might prove useful later. Hero is appalled and asks how Scholar can propose something so vile. The chapter ends with Sunny silently weighing whether he could beat Scholar in a fight, and how much of an obstacle Hero would be.

Hero asks Scholar why Sunny should be the sacrifice instead of Scholar himself, since Scholar looks far closer to the grave. Scholar argues that Sunny already reeks of blood from the veteran's whip, from the slaughter during the attack, and from the dead man's cloak. Hero seems to agree, which terrifies Sunny, but then he smiles and draws his sword. He reveals that he knows exactly who Scholar is, and that he knows the crimes that led to his enslavement. If anyone deserves to be sacrificed, it is Scholar.

Hero breaks both of Scholar's legs and drags him down the path. Sunny is left alone, shaking, and soon hears terrible screams carried by the wind. Hero returns as though nothing happened, takes Scholar's rucksack, and tells Sunny not to feel guilty because the decision was his alone and the killing was an act of justice. Sunny, who despises people who rationalize their cruelty, says nothing.

At sunset they find a hidden cave and decide against a fire because the beast is too close. In the pitch dark, Sunny can see perfectly while Hero is blind. Hero admits that he can usually sense a person's presence even in darkness, but with Sunny there is nothing, as though he were just another shadow. Emboldened by the darkness, Sunny speaks openly for the first time and asks whether Hero is waiting for him to fall asleep before killing him.

Hero admits that he planned to kill Sunny in his sleep so that he wouldn't suffer. He says he is bound by a duty that does not allow him to die, and that dying in the monster's jaws would be a crueler fate than a quick death at his hand. Sunny mocks him for dressing up murder in noble excuses and explains that he decided to survive simply to spite everyone. Hero stands to finish it, but suddenly staggers and vomits blood.

Sunny reveals what he did: after the first attack, while gathering flagons from the dead soldiers, he squeezed Bloodbane juice into every one except his own. Shifty drank the most and thus got sick fastest, and Scholar was dying too before Hero finished him. Sunny says he always expected the others to turn on him, and that Hero is the worst of them, because there is nothing more pathetic than a slave who begins to trust his slaver.

Hero laughs, then reveals that his Soul Core awakened long ago, so the poison cannot kill him. He strikes Sunny, breaking his ribs, and Sunny flees the cave but is caught on the path under the moonlight.

 As Hero raises his sword, Sunny summons the Silver Bell and rings it, and the sound echoes across the mountain before the bell vanishes. Sunny then falls completely silent, staring into the darkness behind Hero.

Sunny's gamble relies on the one advantage he has left: he knows the tyrant is blind and Hero does not. He rang the Silver Bell to draw Mountain King close, and now he stays silent while Hero keeps talking, making himself the only source of noise on the mountain. Too late, Hero realizes what is behind him. Mountain King seizes him and drags him back as Sunny turns and runs uphill, hearing Hero's desperate scream and the monster's roar behind him.

Wounded and freezing, Sunny staggers to the summit, where a ruined temple of black marble stands in the moonlight. Invisible guardians that have killed countless humans and monsters sense the scent of divinity in his soul and let him pass. Fading from hypothermia, he lies down on the altar, and his coughed-up blood is absorbed by the stone. Mountain King follows him into the temple and reaches for him. At that moment the Spell declares: 

[You have offered yourself as a sacrifice to the gods.]

 [The gods are dead, and can not hear you.]

 [You soul bears the mark of divinity.] 

[You are a temple slave.] 

[Shadow God stirs in his eternal slumber.] 

[He sends a blessing from beyond the grave.] 

[Child of Shadows, receive your blessing!]

 The shadows in the hall come alive and tear the tyrant apart.

 The Spell announces that Sunny has slain an awakened tyrant, and tells him that his nightmare is over.

Sunny finds himself in a void of stars and silver strings, which he understands to be the inner workings of the Nightmare Spell. His first reward is a Memory taken from Mountain King, the Puppeteer's Shroud. As an Awakened-rank Memory, it outranks his own dormant Soul Core, which makes it a stroke of great luck. The chapter also lays out the seven ranks of the Spell: Dormant, Awakened, Ascended, Transcendent, Supreme, Sacred, and Divine.

The Spell then delivers its appraisal. It summarizes his ascent of the Black Mountain and credits him with defeating a dormant beast (the Larva), three dormant humans whose names are unknown, an awakened human named Auro of the Nine, and the awakened tyrant Mountain King. It notes that he received the Shadow God's blessing, rates his performance 'glorious,' and adds that his treachery knows no bounds. Sunny is promoted from Aspirant to Dreamer.

He is bestowed a True Name, Lost from Light, and his Temple Slave Aspect evolves into Shadow Slave, which is Divine rank. A Divine Aspect is something he has never heard of anyone obtaining. Its innate ability, Shadow Bond, means that if a master learns his True Name and speaks it aloud, he will be bound to obey every command. Sunny decides he must keep his True Name secret. The chapter ends as the Spell announces that the First Seal is broken and begins awakening his dormant powers.

A strange energy awakens inside Sunny and spreads outward from his chest like a miniature star, rebuilding his bones, muscles, and organs. He feels reborn, and the heat is followed by a soothing cold that sweeps away years of accumulated aches. His eyes seem to double, letting him see both the starry void and his Sea of Soul, a dark, calm sea lit by a lonely black sun.

Things are wrong with it. A Soul Core is supposed to blaze with light, but his sun is dark and transparent, and he senses shapeless forms moving at the edge of his vision. Two spheres of light orbit the sun: his Memories, the Silver Bell and the Puppeteer's Shroud.

The Spell awakens his Aspect Ability, Shadow Control, described only as meaning his shadow is more independent than most and an invaluable helper. Looking over his status, Sunny sees that he has a Shadow Core instead of a Soul Core, and a Shadow Fragments counter, 12 of 1000, in place of the usual soul shard count. He guesses this means he follows a different progression path from all other Awakened, which could make him self-sufficient. The Spell then warns that all power has a price and gives him a Flaw. When Sunny reads it, he is horrified.

Sunny's Flaw is Clear Conscience, and its description is three words: 'You cannot lie.' He is horrified, since his survival has always depended on deceiving others, and he realizes that anyone could learn his True Name just by asking him a question. The Spell then wakes him.

He opens his eyes in the reinforced medical bed in the police station's vault. His injuries are gone and he feels stronger than ever. Sitting beside him is a strikingly beautiful woman with short black hair and icy blue eyes, wearing a uniform with three stars on the insignia. When she asks what he is looking at, his Flaw forces him to answer honestly with embarrassing results, and she slaps him across the room. Sunny keeps blurting out unwanted truths, which amuses her. She tells him that Awakened tend to grow more attractive as their cores develop.

She introduces herself as Ascended Jet, or Master Jet, who has spent the three days of his sleep on watch duty. Sunny learns the terminology: those who finish their First Nightmare are called Sleepers, and the path continues through Awakened, Masters, and Saints. Jet explains that government Awakened are underpaid and few, and when Sunny honestly says he would never do such work out of altruism, she is pleased by his candor. She says he is smarter than he seems.

Master Jet sends Sunny to shower because he reeks of Nightmare. In the mirror he sees that his body is leaner and healthier, though still small. He also notices his reflection's shadow facepalm. When he confronts the shadow, it answers his questions with nods, shrugs, and shakes, proving it acts independently.

Unable to learn more by asking, Sunny looks inward and discovers a new sense that lets him perceive the shapes of nearby shadows through varying pressure, including his own, which feels like a part of his soul. He can command it to move, change shape, or imitate a monster, but as a shadow it cannot touch anything, so it seems far less impressive than the shadow tentacles that killed Mountain King. The shadow looks offended and stops cooperating.

In the cafeteria, Jet briefs him on the formalities. He turns down the free counseling, and she reveals that she also grew up in the outskirts and that few Awakened do. When Jet idly asks what he is thinking, the Flaw drags a truthful answer out of him. She tells him he is free to prepare for the Dream Realm however he likes, but recommends the Awakened Academy for free lodging, classes, and the chance to meet future companions. Sunny, who has about four weeks until the winter solstice, accepts.

Sunny waits outside the red gates of the Awakened Academy, a fortress-like city within the city that features in countless youth dramas and webtoons. He has only four weeks before the Dream Realm and plans to focus on learning to survive. With him is another new Sleeper, a tall, slender girl with short silver-white hair, clear grey eyes, and old-fashioned headphones. She is wearing the same police-issued tracksuit, listens to music, and seems apart from the world. Sunny avoids speaking to her because of his Flaw.

The chapter recalls Master Jet's drive to the Academy and her three pieces of advice. First, refuse the psychological counseling the Academy offers in exchange for soul shards, because in the Dream Realm humans become as dangerous as monsters, and knowledge of his Aspect could be used against him through his Flaw. Second, ignore the combat and sorcery courses and take only Wilderness Survival, since Sunny only knows how to survive in the city, and it was the cold that nearly killed him in the Nightmare. Third, remember that no one survives the Dream Realm alone, so he should try to get along with his peers.

Jet drops him at the gates and leaves with a smile and a warning to stay alive. The bridge lowers and the silver-haired girl walks forward, and Sunny follows reluctantly.

Sunny and the silver-haired girl are led to the Sleepers' building, where about a hundred young Sleepers wait for the induction ceremony. Everyone is well-dressed, carries luggage, and is strikingly attractive, which makes the two arrivals in plain police clothes conspicuous. The room is full of people who want to talk about their Nightmares, and for someone who cannot keep quiet or lie, this is a disaster.

Within half an hour, nearly everyone hates him. His honest answers make him look like a rude, arrogant pervert, and he is slapped several times and punched once. Left alone in a corner with a bloody nose, he realizes something useful: although he cannot lie, he can influence how his truthful answers are worded, at the cost of increasing pressure and pain. He reasons that two true statements placed together can mislead as well as a lie, as when he told someone he took a dead man's boots and cloak, which implied he killed for them.

He decides to use this to hide his True Name by making everyone believe he is pathetic and has an unimpressive record. He singles out a tall, handsome young man with brown hair and green eyes who is surrounded by admirers after revealing his Ascended Aspect with an 'excellent' appraisal. Sunny walks up and asks, with apparent bewilderment, what the big deal is about an Ascended Aspect and an excellent appraisal.

Sunny's dismissal of Caster's Ascended Aspect leaves the group of Sleepers stunned. Caster only smiles politely, but Sunny notices a calculating coldness in his eyes that reminds him of Hero. The street gangs of the outskirts call it 'murder math,' the habit of seasoned fighters to always be calculating how to kill the person in front of them. One of Caster's companions explains that Caster is a Legacy, a descendant of an Awakened clan trained for the Spell since birth, which makes his results truly remarkable.

Sunny keeps up the act. When asked about his own Appraisal, he says it was 'glorious' and that his Aspect is Divine rank, then boasts that he killed an awakened tyrant by spitting on it, killed an awakened swordsman by shaking a finger, and was blessed by a god. Each statement is technically true.

The Sleepers laugh and decide he is insane. Caster stops them, asks what else he achieved, and then gently says that Sunny's accomplishments make his own look average. Sunny leaves feeling triumphant, sure that nobody will ever believe his true Aspect or True Name.

 As he walks away, he overhears Caster telling his companions that the poor kid probably lost his mind in the Nightmare and will likely die soon, so kindness is the least he can offer.

Sunny retreats to the deserted corner of the hall, where the only person sitting is a delicate, doll-like girl with pale blond hair and big blue eyes. Her empty stare reminds him of Mountain King, and he realizes she is blind. Since she could not have survived the First Nightmare blind, he concludes that her blindness is her Flaw, and a blind person has almost no chance of surviving the Dream Realm with a dormant core. Sunny sees her as a walking corpse, and understands why other Sleepers keep away from the corner.

Looking at the room, he sees that the Sleepers have sorted themselves by circumstance. Near the stage are the Legacies, who are confident and ready, with Caster standing out. Next come the scions of rich and powerful families, then the largest group of middle-class kids with decent schooling and a fair chance. Last are Sunny and the blind girl, the 'corpses' with almost no chance of survival. The silver-haired girl stands alone, eyes closed, listening to music, apart from every group.

A giant of a man with a brown beard and a dark blue uniform takes the stage and introduces himself as Awakened Rock. He tells the Sleepers that they are not as ready as they think, that the Spell is merciless, that even Masters and Saints die, and that their survival rests on them alone. His speech is meant to frighten them, since fear is what will keep them alive, and he then moves on to the difference between Nightmares and the Dream Realm.

Awakened Rock explains the difference between Nightmares and the Dream Realm. First Nightmares are individual, so only one Creature can cross over if the Sleeper dies. From the Second Nightmare on, Nightmares are born in the Dream Realm, and if no Awakened find and destroy the Seed before it matures, a Gate opens in the real world and lets monsters through. Gates have ranks of their own, and a Rank 5 Gate once left an entire continent uninhabitable. Closing maturing Nightmares is the Awakened's main purpose. If Nightmares are the destination, the Dream Realm is the road.

He describes the Dream Realm as a vast, mostly unexplored and dead world, home only to Nightmare Creatures and ruins of lost civilizations. It is unknown whether it is real or an illusion of the Spell, but the Nightmares seem to replay historical events, which makes Sunny wonder about the nameless slave and about Hero's fate. Rock lists four differences. There is no predetermined story, so Sleepers can move freely. There are no people except the Awakened who entered, and some Creatures can mimic humans. Death in the Dream Realm does not send a Creature into the real world. And there is no fairness limit, so a Sleeper could meet an Unholy Titan anywhere.

On the solstice they will be drawn in at an unpredictable location, and Rock advises them to band together and reach the nearest human Citadel. Each is built around a Gateway, which lets them return as Awakened with evolved cores and a second Aspect Ability. If there is no Citadel, they should search for an unclaimed Gateway near a major landmark. Sunny, with his [Fated] Attribute, doubts he will get an easy placement, and dismisses the group to dormitories, supper, and interviews.

chapters.chapter_title: Chapter 24: Moving Up in the World
chapters.chapter_summary:
Sunny is stunned to receive a private dormitory with a soft bed, a bathroom, a screen imitating a snowy park, and free Academy clothes. To someone from the outskirts it feels like a palace. He finally reads the description of the Puppeteer's Shroud, an Awakened-rank armor made from the black silk cocoon of a Puppeteer Worm that once devoured a king from the inside. When summoned, it forms a light, silent armor of dark-grey cloth and black leather that gives him a faint calm and probably protects against mental attacks, and it makes him wonder what Mountain King, the mature worm, would have become as a moth.

Supper at the Academy cafeteria includes unlimited real meat, and he eats happily. In his interview he refuses counseling again and answers carefully, giving only enough information to suggest that his Aspect is weak, harmless, and probably utility-based. He sleeps soundly for the first time in a long while.

Next morning the only free seat at breakfast is beside the blind girl and the social worker who helps her. A crowd is gathered around a screen showing the new batch ranked from weakest to strongest. Sunny sees his own name near the bottom, with only the blind girl, whose name is Cassia, below him.

The commotion is about the top of the list. Caster is second, and first is the silver-haired girl, listed as 'Name: Nephis' and 'True Name: Changing Star.'

Sunny is struck that Nephis also received a True Name in her First Nightmare, and he has to resist the urge to announce that he has one too. The cafeteria is in uproar. Some Sleepers doubt it is possible, citing Smile of Heaven as a rare exception, and others suggest that she lied in her interview. Caster seems to be staring at the line reading 'Nephis' instead of the True Name, as if her real name meant more to him.

He then walks over, bows, and introduces himself to her as 'Caster of the Han Li clan,' calling her 'Lady Nephis.' She answers his polite question about her trial with a bright smile and a shrug, 'It is what it is,' and returns to her coffee. Sunny wonders how they are connected, then forgets about it and goes back to his breakfast.

In the Wilderness Survival classroom he finds only one person, Awakened Julius, a lively old man with bushy eyebrows who is delighted to have a student in a course the other Sleepers ignore. When Sunny says Master Jet recommended the class, Julius reacts in horror and calls her 'Soul Reaper Jet.' He says her Aspect Abilities strike soul cores directly and bypass armor. He adds that her personality makes it unlikely she will ever receive help to become a Saint, then catches himself for gossiping. Sunny signs up for nothing else.

Julius's curriculum is vast, covering theory, virtual reality and real-world drills, and even dead languages of the Dream Realm, since the Spell does not translate everything. After a draining day, Sunny returns to his room and turns to experiment with his shadow.

Sunny practices Shadow Control until it feels as natural as walking. He discovers that the shadow can detach from his feet and move around the room, and that he can focus his perception through it so he sees two pictures at once, his own and the shadow's. Together with his Child of Shadows Attribute, this makes him an ideal spy and scout.

 His shadow slips under the door and glides down the hall, and Sunny stops it at the corner leading to the girls' dormitory and decides against exploring, since with his reputation he needs to be able to say honestly that he did not do anything improper.

He sends it instead into a combat class led by Instructor Rock. Rock tests each Sleeper's striking strength on a machine. Most score between ten and fourteen, those with enhancing Aspects reach fifteen or sixteen, and Nephis scores sixteen. Caster's punch is too fast to see and scores twenty-one.

 In the sparring that follows, Nephis volunteers first and then defeats nearly every Sleeper in the dojo with efficient technique, never changing her calm expression. Watching, Sunny is unsettled and decides that he never wants Changing Star as an enemy. Finally, only Caster remains. He steps into the ring, bows to Nephis, and asks her to excuse him in advance.

Caster moves too fast for most eyes. Sunny catches it only because of Shadow Sight. Nephis deflects the first blow but still takes a hit to the shoulder, then feints toward where Caster was and drives an elbow back as he circles behind her. He dodges by a hair, trips her, and then catches her collar so she lands gently. The whole fight lasts about two seconds.

 Sunny concludes that an Ascended Aspect is cheating, but notices that Nephis never used her Aspect Ability against Caster, or at any point that day, so no one knows what it is. Despite that, Caster barely managed to win, and he looks troubled instead of pleased.

In the locker room, Sunny's shadow listens as Caster's admirers praise him and dismiss Nephis. Caster snaps at another Legacy who calls her a peasant girl and reveals that she is Nephis of the Immortal Flame clan, whose parents were Smile of Heaven and Broken Sword.

 Immortal Flame was the first human to conquer the Second Nightmare and Broken Sword the first to conquer the Third. The Legacy asks why she arrived with nothing, and Caster explains that the clan is gone and she is the only one left.

Late that night, Sunny sneaks into the dojo and punches the machine, scoring only nine. In frustration he strikes again, and his shadow instinctively wraps around his fist like a glove, raising the score to eighteen.

Days pass in a blur as Sunny fills every hour with training. By day he studies with Teacher Julius, learning fire-making, celestial navigation, and the dead languages of the Dream Realm. The lessons also teach him why things work as they do, since Julius goes into much more depth than textbooks. Knowing the rune language helps him understand the Spell better. Nephis's True Name, translated as 'Changing Star,' could more accurately be read as 'Star of Change,' and depending on which rune for 'change' is used, it could even mean 'Ruinous Star' or 'Star of Misfortune.'

Sunny reflects that knowledge is the privilege of the wealthy and the cause of a cycle of inequality, and he is now one of those privileged by government support for food and shelter. Practical lessons every other day, in virtual reality and the real world, leave him exhausted but in the best shape of his life, as his rebirth has pushed his body to the peak of what is humanly possible.

At night he continues to train with Shadow Control and gathers information about other Sleepers by sending his shadow to observe classes and listen to conversations. It is capable, but naive, and often brings back gossip instead of useful secrets, which is how he learns that romance is blooming among the Sleepers. Sunny keeps to himself, wary of any closeness that might force him to reveal his True Name. He also learns that his shadow can double the power of weapons and armor it wraps around. Before he knows it, the winter solstice has arrived.

chapters.chapter_title: Chapter 29: The Last Day on Earth
chapters.chapter_summary:
On the day of the solstice Sunny wakes up feeling the same heavy sleepiness he felt before his First Nightmare. He tells himself he is as ready as he can be. The cafeteria is silent, with only the Legacies calm. He tries coffee again, this time with sugar and milk. At the table, the blind girl Cassia unexpectedly turns toward him and says 'Happy Birthday.' Sunny had forgotten that he is turning seventeen, and he is unsettled that she knew. He says thanks, and spends a moment thinking about the people who used to celebrate his birthdays with him.

He says goodbye to Teacher Julius, who gives him a dozen 'one last tips' and promises to apply for a research assistant position once Sunny is Awakened. At sunset, Instructor Rock leads the Sleepers to the Academy medical center, where their bodies will be kept in pods and sustained by Healers. First, Rock takes them to a gallery of wheelchairs holding silent, empty people called the Hollow, who were once Sleepers or Awakened and whose souls were destroyed in the Dream Realm. He looks toward Caster and Nephis and tells the group not to die out there.

In separate rooms, Cassia weeps as she tries to navigate by touch, Caster stares at the floor and repeats a strange phrase, and Nephis looks at her hands as a white glow grows under her skin and her face twists in pain. Sunny asks his shadow if it is ready, then climbs into the pod. The Spell welcomes him to the Dream Realm.

Instead of seeing a preview, as he did at the start of his First Nightmare, Sunny finds himself blind and drowning in salt water in total darkness. His Child of Shadows sight fails, but his shadow perception lets him tell up from down. He swims to the surface, and sees an endless black sea under a sky with no moon or stars.

 A huge dorsal fin about five meters tall approaches from hundreds of meters away, and he swims for a black mass jutting from the water, using his shadow to double his speed. He reaches it just before the creature, climbs up, and watches as enormous jaws with teeth as long as he is tall strike the rock. Then a giant black tentacle rises from the sea and drags the creature under. Sunny realizes the monster was fleeing, not hunting him.

The mass is a man-made-looking stone platform about twelve meters across, with grooves in its surface, floating alone in the sea. Sunny is cold, wet, and naked, so he summons the Puppeteer's Shroud for clothes and boots. He cannot match the place to any known region of the Dream Realm, and he decides to wait. He thanks his barely visible shadow for its help, and lies down. Hours later, the sky greys, a pale sun begins to rise, and the dark sea suddenly surges.

As the pale sun rises, the black sea begins to recede. Soon Sunny finds himself standing on the top of a cliff more than a hundred meters high, and a labyrinth of crimson coral emerges from the water, stretching in every direction. He sends his shadow down the cliff to explore, and jokes about giving it a name, suggesting Shameless or Shady, but gets no answer. The labyrinth is confusing, multi-layered, and full of bones buried in the mud.

The shadow circles the cliff and finds the half-eaten corpse of the shark-like creature that chased Sunny the night before, with its other half missing. Hundreds of pincer-armed monsters, each about two and a half meters tall, are feasting on it. They look like a mix of demonic crab and centaur, with four pairs of scythe-like legs, a human-like torso, and two large pincers, and they fight each other over choice pieces.

Studying the cliff, Sunny realizes it is a colossal statue, at least two hundred meters tall, of a knight in plate armor with seven shining stars on the breastplate, holding a huge sword point-down. The head has been torn off, and the platform he is standing on is the top of its neck. At sunset a rumble sounds, the monsters flee into the coral or bury themselves in the mud, and the sea floods back, leaving the platform as the only dry spot.

In the middle of the night, Sunny's shadow wakes him and points to a small orange light shimmering a few kilometers away. It vanishes before he can figure out what it is. Hunger and thirst keep him awake. In the morning he sees a hill with a huge coral pillar five or six kilometers away, high enough to stay above the water at night, which is probably where the light came from. Sunny weighs his options. He could survive by staying near the statue, desalinating seawater and hunting scavengers by day, but that offers no hope of improvement and he would sooner end it than live that way. He decides to try to reach the hill the next morning.

A storm hits that night, and he drinks rainwater from his cupped hands, grinning, and holds on to the grooves of the stone as waves crash over the platform. In the morning, he climbs down the statue using climbing skills Teacher Julius taught him and a route his shadow has scouted. He enters the labyrinth, feeling better for taking action, and the shadow scouts ahead. The labyrinth seems endless, and he has to backtrack more than once. He notices that the mud contains many bones. Overconfident in his preparation, he lowers his guard, and a huge pincer suddenly bursts from the mud in front of him.

Sunny falls backward as the pincer snaps shut inches from his face, then rolls away from the follow-up strike. The attacker is one of the pincer monsters, almost three meters tall, but it is badly wounded, with half of its eight legs broken, cracks in its carapace leaking blue blood, and one pincer torn off. That is why it was lying in ambush instead of feasting with the others. His shadow had passed over its trap earlier without alerting it, because it is weightless and silent.

Sunny recalls his shadow, pulls a sharp, spear-like bone from the mud, and tries to keep away from the creature, but a pincer grazes his leg and knocks him down. The Puppeteer's Shroud keeps it from drawing blood. Realizing he cannot outrun it, he decides on a crazy plan and lets the monster grab him across the torso. The Shroud resists the crushing, and his shadow wraps around the armor to strengthen it further. As the monster lifts him toward its mandibles, he lets his shadow flow onto the bone and drives it through the creature's eye, twisting it. The monster collapses. The Spell announces that he has slain an awakened beast, a Carapace Scavenger, and that he has received a Memory called the Azure Blade.

After the fight, Sunny sees that his Shadow Fragments have gone up to 14 of 1000. He works out how they work. Killing a dormant enemy gives one fragment and an awakened one gives two, and only kills he makes himself count. The twelve he started with came from the Larva, the veteran slaver, and the five cores of Mountain King. He gets none for Shifty, Scholar, or Hero. Fragments cannot be stored, bought, or traded, so he can only grow by killing. The upside is that he can keep and spend the soul shards that every kill leaves behind, and since the shadow is tied to his Shadow Core, strengthening the core improves both of them.

He reads the description of the Azure Blade, 'On this forgotten shore, only steel remembers,' and summons it, a light single-edged sword with deep white sparks in the blade. When his shadow wraps around it, it turns bluish-black like a starry sky. Sunny carves meat from the scavenger and takes its soul shard, which is of no use to him directly, then limps on with a banged-up leg while the sea's return approaches. Just when he begins to despair of reaching the hill, his shadow sees a clearing where Nephis, dressed only in seaweed, is walking with a golden rope, at the other end of which Cassia follows.

chapters.chapter_title: Chapter 35: A Shadow, a Star and an Oracle
chapters.chapter_summary:
Sunny watches the two girls, Nephis with her silver hair and crude seaweed clothes, and Cassia in a tunic and sea-colored cloak, and realizes that if they were the source of the orange light, they know the way to the hill. He is worried about approaching them, since he has just spent four weeks making sure everyone at the Academy hated him. He decides to send his shadow into view first, but Nephis summons a sword and aims it at the shadow immediately. When she tells Cassia that it is a human shadow and that it is waving at them, Sunny speaks up from hiding.

When she calls him a creep for hiding, his Flaw makes him say he is a little afraid of her, and he deliberately adds her True Name so they will know he is not a monster in disguise. Cassia recognizes his voice as the boy from the cafeteria, and Nephis asks, 'The pervert?' Sunny protests that it was all a misunderstanding. She lowers the sword and tells him to come out. When he explains that his injuries come from killing a Carapace Scavenger, adding that it was already wounded, Nephis says a kill is a kill. Cassia says that they have been staying on the hill and are heading back, and when Sunny asks to come along, Nephis hesitates, then says 'No… problem.'

With Nephis leading and Sunny holding Cassia's rope, they reach the hill in time. Sunny silently thinks that Cassia is dead weight, since she cannot walk the labyrinth properly even with her staff, and wonders why Nephis is risking so much. At the coral pillar, Nephis dismisses and re-summons the golden rope, a Memory that can lengthen itself, ties it around a protrusion at the top, climbs up, and signals Sunny to follow. He fears a trap at first, then reasons that she would not need one. Cassia climbs by stepping into a loop at the end of the rope while Nephis hauls her up.

Their small camp on the top of the mound has seaweed beds, drying scavenger meat, and a firepit. Cassia says that when they lit their first fire two nights ago, scavengers came and then the giant tentacle. She lends Sunny a Memory, a beautiful blue glass bottle that is always full, and he drinks gratefully. When Nephis finds a soul shard in his rucksack, she looks at it, then puts it back and does not ask about it. Sunny describes the headless statue and the carcass the scavengers are devouring, which explains why they are scarce in the daytime. Nephis asks how long until they finish, and he says one or two days. As night falls and they eat, Cassia suggests that they introduce themselves properly. She is Cassie, the other is Neph, and he tells them to call him Sunny.

chapters.chapter_title: Chapter 37: Getting to Know Each Other
chapters.chapter_summary:
Sunny, who finds conversation in the dark easier, proposes that they share their abilities and Memories. He goes first so he controls what he reveals. He tells them his Attributes give him an affinity to shadows, a slight affiliation to divinity, and a tendency to end up in unlikely situations. Cassie says he is telling the truth, explaining that her Ability lets her see people's Attributes and sometimes receive visions of the past or future. Sunny realizes that this is how she knew his birthday, and decides he must be careful around her. He then describes his Shadow Scout and his dark vision, and when the girls look alarmed he quickly insists he never used it improperly in the Academy, mentioning that he was studying Wilderness Survival while Nephis was beating up other Sleepers. Nephis admits that she did not know the class existed.

Nephis says that her Attributes give her an affinity to light and fire and a strong affiliation to divinity, and that she has two Memories, a rope and a sword that can protect against soul attacks. Her Ability 'can be used to heal.' Sunny notes the wording. Cassie lists a bottle, a staff that can create wind, and an Awakened-rank armor that Nephis gave her, and says she used to be a decent fencer, but can't fight now. Nobody shares their Flaw. Nephis insists on taking the first watch, even after Sunny offers his shadow.

Unable to sleep, Sunny asks Nephis why she had so few Memories for a Legacy. She says she started with only two, since the rope is Cassie's. Her clan lost most of its Memories when her father died, and the rest were sold over the years, while the sword and armor came from her First Nightmare. When she asks how he knew she is a Legacy, he says he heard Caster mention it. Then he asks why she burdens herself with Cassie. She asks if he wouldn't, and the Flaw makes him answer 'No.' Nephis only says, 'Because I want to,' and Sunny realizes that he has always done things because he must, and that she might have the freedom to do things just because she wants to.

Nephis then asks if he knows the legend of Odysseus. She tells of the Trojan War heroes Achilles, Diomedes, and Ajax, and of Odysseus, the cunning one, who wandered after the war and ended up on the island of the fairy Calypso, where he had paradise and immortality but left on a makeshift boat. She asks why. Sunny guesses it was because he was far from home. She says that he returned to his family, and adds quietly that Odysseus was the first human to break the will of gods.

In the morning they plan to go east, away from the scavengers, when Cassie wakes from a vision of a castle full of people, and points west.

Sunny points out that the direction Cassie indicated is exactly where the scavengers are. Nephis asks her to describe the vision. Cassie saw a vast ruined city of weathered stone within tall walls and full of monsters, with a hill at its center and a magnificent castle on top that was full of Awakened, safe and living in comfort, with food and laughter. She also saw Sunny leading her through the castle gates. Sunny notices that she mentioned only the two of them, and wonders whether Nephis noticed. After thinking, Nephis says they will go west.

While they prepare, Sunny has a realization about Nephis. Her silence, strange phrasing, and cold face, which he took for mysterious aloofness, are really awkwardness. She cannot speak naturally or show emotion, so she speaks little and her tone often does not match her meaning. He is shocked, since he assumed she was a protagonist type, but concludes that it does not make her any less dangerous. When she notices him staring and says 'What?', he covers by asking when they leave, and she answers 'Soon.'

They head west in the gray morning, with Nephis in front, Sunny holding the rope that guides Cassie, and his shadow scouting ahead. It soon runs into a group of hungry scavengers.

The shadow finds six scavengers on the path ahead, apparently stragglers who could not find room at the carcass. Nephis leads them around them, but over the next hour they keep having to change paths as more scavengers appear, and they are making no progress toward the statue. Cassie suggests turning back, but Nephis points out that tomorrow will be harder, and says they must fight. Sunny objects that each scavenger is a rank above them. Nephis says that they will avoid large groups and take on small ones.

She asks whether he studied the scavenger he killed, and then lists three weak points. They're hard to reach, so Nephis will bait the monster and make it turn while Sunny strikes. When he asks what to do if there are two, she says, 'Don't die.'

With no other way forward, they leave Cassie against a wall and meet a lone scavenger in a clearing. Nephis dodges and counters, cutting a leg joint, and maneuvers it so its back faces Sunny's hiding place. He leaps onto its carapace and drives the shadow-wrapped Azure Blade into the weak point. The scavenger falls, and the Spell announces the kill.

The fight is over in under ten seconds, and Sunny checks his Shadow Fragments, now 16 of 1000. Nephis did most of the work, but he dealt the killing blow. He remembers Master Jet's advice that no one can survive in the Dream Realm alone and begins to see that depending on a group is not weakness but part of strength. Together, they killed a scavenger that either one would have struggled with alone.

When Nephis asks if he got a Memory and he says no, Sunny fetches Cassie, thinking of his little sister as the blind girl follows behind him. Nephis tosses him the soul shard because, she says, she has no pockets, and promises to divide the spoils later. Over the day they kill three more scavengers the same way, with Nephis acting as bait and Sunny, hidden by shadows and his shadow's scouting, delivering the finishing blow. Watching her fight without using her Aspect Ability teaches him how much more skill matters than raw power. His fragments rise to 22 of 1000.

At sunset they cross to the statue, and the three of them take turns hauling Cassie up the two-hundred-meter climb with the rope, reaching the top just before the sea returns. Nephis divides the four soul shards, two for her, one for Cassie, and one for Sunny. Sunny instead gives her all of his shards, and offers to give her every soul shard he earns on the way to the castle, in return for her teaching him how to fight.

Nephis takes a long time to weigh the offer. Sunny knows she is judging his current ability and future potential from what she has seen. She accepts the soul shards and says, 'Okay.' She starts the lessons right away, though only with words, since it is almost dark, and tells Cassie to listen as well.

She says mastery of combat has two parts, the body and the mind. The body is trained through repetition and then cemented through real experience, since a thousand hours of training matter less than one real fight. Sunny wonders what kind of life gave her so much battle experience at eighteen. The mind is harder, and the first step is to understand the essence of combat. When Cassie guesses victory and Sunny guesses survival, Nephis says no, the essence of combat is murder. One person is trying to kill the other, and everything else, including style, weapons, reason, and intent, is noise. Everything done in a fight either serves to kill the enemy or to stop the enemy from killing you.

Sunny lies awake afterward, thinking about repetition, experience, and clarity. He sees that the lesson matches what he has known all his life in the outskirts, and he wonders if that makes him better suited to being an Awakened than most. Early in the morning, a piercing scream wakes him.

Sunny wakes with the Azure Blade already in his hand and sees Cassie stumbling at the edge of the platform with a horrified expression and her hands outstretched. He runs, without thinking, and catches her just before she steps into the dark water, holding her tightly and telling her everything is fine. There is no sign of danger anywhere, and Cassie has no injuries. She manages only a few words, 'the head… I saw… oh gods!' before going silent. Sunny and Nephis cannot get anything more from her, and Nephis suggests leaving her alone.

As the sun rises, Nephis moves Sunny to the edge of the platform, keeping Cassie in sight, and says that Cassie is strong. She compares the two swords, explaining that his is meant for cutting with both hands and hers is a longsword for both cutting and thrusting, but that both are leverage weapons in which one hand pushes and the other pulls. She also tells him that a strike comes from the feet, hips, core, and shoulders, not the hands. After correcting his form, she tells him to repeat the downward slash a thousand more times, and he does, repeating 'Repetition, experience, clarity' to himself until he is done. By then, Cassie is ready to speak.

Sore from the thousand strikes, Sunny sits down beside Cassie, who is pale and dazed but no longer trembling. After sharing the water bottle, she describes her dream, which she thinks may have been a nightmare. She saw a boundless darkness locked behind seven seals, with something vast churning inside, and the seals broke one by one until the last one broke too. Then her mind shattered into many images. She saw the human castle again at night, burning under a lonely star with rivers of blood flowing through its halls, a corpse in golden armor on a throne, a woman with a bronze spear drowning in a tide of monsters, and an archer trying to pierce the falling sky with arrows. Finally, she saw a crimson spire with seven severed heads guarding seven locks and, at its top, a dying angel being consumed by shadows. She felt something infinitely precious taken from her, and woke full of sorrow and rage.

Sunny suggests it might be a side effect of her Ability, but privately finds the angel ominous. Later, watching the scavengers finish the shark carcass, the three see two luminous crystals in the bones, shards from two transcendent soul cores. Nephis says the shark must have been a corrupted devil, which makes Sunny realize he was closer to death than he thought. Then two much larger monsters appear, black and scarlet with spiked carapaces and bone scythes instead of pincers. Scavengers flee from them, and each monster takes one shard and carries it away. Nephis decides to leave the next day and tells Sunny to send his shadow to follow them.

Sunny's shadow, whose range has grown a little with the extra fragments, can only tell that the two large monsters went west. He rests while Nephis meditates. Cassie asks him if he thinks they will make it home, and Sunny says yes, because of Nephis and because he is not easy to kill either. When she teases him about ranking second to last, he jokes that he would have been third to last if he had not been told to keep a low profile, and she laughs, the first time he has heard her laugh.

She then asks what he misses most about home. He says nothing in particular, that he has no family apart from a sister he has not seen in years, and she says she misses her family the most, and that her parents would be heartbroken, not just worried. When she asks if it is not normal to care about family, Sunny says he would not know.

That evening and morning he again does a thousand strikes. At dawn, Nephis tells them that there will be far more scavengers in the labyrinth and tells Sunny to take Cassie away if they get into trouble, and to continue on alone if they are separated. As they move, they end up with a large group of scavengers behind them and two blocking the path ahead. Nephis decides they can take two, and steps forward to attack first.

After hiding Cassie, Sunny and Nephis go after the two scavengers. Nephis sprints so fast that Sunny falls behind, then drops and slides through the mud between the two monsters, stopping herself with her sword. Sunny follows through the shadows and leaps from the coral wall to strike the weak point of the second scavenger, but it turns at the last moment and his blade slides off the armor. He lands on its back, is thrown against the wall, and rolls aside as a pincer shatters the coral.

He wraps himself in shadow and, remembering what Nephis taught him, makes himself charge toward the scavenger instead of away. He slashes down with a push-and-pull stroke, cutting off a front leg at the joint, and when the creature loses its balance, he thrusts the sword into its mouth. The scavenger dies on the blade. Sunny's head is bleeding from the impact. By the time he reaches Nephis, she has killed the other scavenger by severing its spine. A gash on her shoulder is minor, but her seaweed top has come apart, and she tells him not to come closer. He turns away, flustered.

Back with Cassie, Nephis has repaired her top. She checks his head wound and asks if he received a Memory. When he checks his runes, he finds none, but he sees a new line under Echoes: Carapace Scavenger.

Sunny can hardly believe that he got an Echo, a type of reward that is rarer and more valuable than a Memory. In his Sea of Soul, he finds it as a larger sphere of light, which he lowers to the water until it takes shape as a Carapace Scavenger. Its runes read Echo Type: Beast, Echo Core: Awakened, Echo Attributes: [Strong], [Armored], with the description 'A cursed soldier of the fallen legion.' As an Awakened Echo, it is a rank above him. When he touches it, a prompt appears asking if he wants to transform the Echo into a Shadow, which he has never heard of. He says yes, but is told he does not have enough Shadow Fragments, with a requirement of 100 and a current count of 24. He decides to focus on strengthening himself for now.

He tells Nephis and Cassie, and summons the Scavenger, which he assigns to carry Cassie. The golden rope becomes makeshift reins. With this speed they move faster, and Sunny feels calm for the first time in this world.

Then the wind picks up and Cassie asks them to stop. She cannot hear anything, so she gets down and puts her ear to the ground, and says that it is murmuring. A drop of water lands on Sunny's face, and he looks up to see storm clouds gathering at unnatural speed, about to cover the sun.

Sunny realizes what a storm means for the sea and urges Nephis to move. His shadow, sent up a pillar, shows the cliffs three or four kilometers away, with the statue much too far behind to return to. Nephis says that it might be possible by the most direct route, cutting through whatever monsters are in the way. They run, with Sunny leading using his shadow's scouting and the Scavenger carrying Cassie behind them.

The rain grows into a downpour, the wind howls, and the light dims to twilight. The scavengers are panicked themselves, hiding in coral or burrowing, and a pincer clack or a sword flash is enough to turn aside any that show aggression. Thunder shakes the ground and Sunny falls, but Nephis hauls him up and shouts for him to keep running. Soon the black water is at his shins, then his waist, slowing them. They reach the cliffs just as a huge wall of water roars through the labyrinth, bursting a late scavenger's carapace like an egg.

Nephis tells Sunny to dismiss the Echo, ties Cassie to her back with the rope, and begins to climb. A surge hits just below them, and the sea keeps rising. Sunny's grip fails when the water reaches his shoulders and the current tears him away, but Nephis drops the golden rope next to him in the last second. He climbs with its help, and she pulls him over the top. All three are alive.

As the three lie exhausted on the top of the cliffs in the rain, Sunny's shadow keeps pulling at his attention. It is warning him about something. He stands, and Nephis asks what is wrong. He cannot see any danger at first. The upper cliff is a small island with rough ridges, with large piles of dirt and tall boulders scattered around. When lightning flashes, he sees that the boulders are not stones. They are scavengers, eight of them, lying silent in the dark. They are also sheltering from the sea, and the three humans are surrounded.

He tells Nephis and Cassie to stay still and silent. Realizing that the monsters have not attacked, perhaps because they are waiting out the storm, he decides that the darkness and noise of the storm favor a shadow, and tells them that he will take care of it. He moves unseen and silent through the dark, feeling calm and in his element. He picks the monster farthest from the others, circles it, jumps onto its carapace, and drives the Azure Blade into the weak spot at its back.

He does not hear the Spell announce a kill or any shadow fragments. When he looks again at the scavenger, he sees that it is already dead, and his face goes pale.

The scavenger Sunny stabbed was already dead. Its carapace had been cut open from the top of the torso to the legs, hidden by the rain, and its organs were spilling out. As he checks the other seven, he finds all of them dead, one nearly severed in half. The dark has stopped being comforting and has become terrifying.

He decides he cannot leave the unknown killer a mystery, and climbs a stone ridge to look. A few meters below him is a large silhouette with spikes growing from its black and crimson carapace and two bone scythes where its pincers should be. It is one of the monsters that took the transcendent soul shards. He climbs back down, shaking, and returns to Nephis and Cassie to report that the killer is an awakened monster sheltering under the ridge.

Nephis says to kill it. She explains that they cannot leave the cliffs before morning, neither can the monster, and in daylight it will see them and the element of surprise will be gone. They are not ordinary Sleepers, she says, and with Sunny, his Echo, and an ambush they have a good chance. Cassie adds that their main advantage is that they are intelligent and the monster is not. Sunny concedes that the fight is inevitable. Some time later he stands in the dark, gripping the Azure Blade, with an ominous feeling, and raises his hand.

Betting that the monster's intelligence is only beastly cunning, the three finalize a plan. Sunny collects the soul shards from the eight dead scavengers, and Nephis crushes them one by one to absorb them, which is equivalent to killing sixteen dormant creatures. Cassie tells Nephis to go and find something decent to wear. Sunny stands on the ridge above the monster, feeling that this will not end well, and rings the Silver Bell.

The monster turns on him with a mad light in its eyes, and Sunny jumps off the ridge and runs as it smashes through the rock behind him. He passes beneath the golden rope that Nephis has strung between two boulders at leg height, and the monster, overcome by bloodlust, runs into it at full speed. The boulders shatter, but its legs are jerked back and it falls. Sunny's Echo, which has been pretending to be one of the dead scavengers, leaps onto its back and pins its arms below the scythes. Nephis appears and drives her longsword deep into the gap between carapace and torso, but the monster barely notices. It throws the Echo off and rises, and Nephis, now weaponless, dives under its body.

Sunny slashes a rear leg but cannot sever it. The monster spins and a bone scythe hits his chest, and only the shadow wrapped around the Puppeteer's Shroud keeps it from piercing his heart. His ribcage caves in, and he lands on the ground drowning in blood, unable to move, as two crimson eyes approach through the dark.

As Sunny lies dying, his mind fogged, he refuses to give the world the satisfaction of his death, remembering his vow to Hero to survive. He grabs for an anchor and remembers Nephis's lesson of repetition, experience, and clarity, and the essence of combat as murder. Rebuilding his mind around that truth, he suddenly thinks clearly and quickly. His body is useless and the shadow is busy keeping him alive, so the only tool left is the Echo.

As the monster looms over him and raises its scythes, the Echo rams it from the side. They tangle in a violent struggle in which the Echo's pincer arm is cut off, and the monster throws it away, breaking one of its own wounded rear legs in the process. The monster rises, and at that moment lightning strikes the handle of Nephis's longsword, still sticking out of its body, electrocuting it. The crimson patterns on its carapace turn white and glowing.

The monster staggers up, but Nephis grabs the hot hilt, twists it, and pulls it out, then severs one of its scythe arms with the glowing blade. It swats her away, and as it lunges toward her, the Echo steps in front of it and plunges its remaining pincer deep into the gap in the armor, tearing the torso off the carapace. The Spell announces that Sunny has slain an awakened monster, a Carapace Centurion, and has received the Memory Starlight Legion Armor. Sunny dismisses the Echo and his consciousness fades as Nephis's hands touch his face.

Sunny sees Nephis kneeling beside him, frightened but resigned. She presses her hands against his caved-in chest and a white radiance ignites beneath her skin. Her face contorts and she screams, bleeding from her bitten lip, while Sunny feels nothing but warmth as a pure white flame rebuilds his bones, flesh, lungs, and heart. When he draws a breath, she crawls away, vomits, and lies shaking, catching raindrops in her mouth. He is completely healed.

The three sleep through the end of the storm and the night. In the morning, they collect meat and the centurion's two soul shards and move to the other side of the island. A huge creature then lands beside the corpse, white as a corpse with a lion's body, six forelimbs, black feathers, and a raven's head and beak. It eats the centurion, takes a few scavenger carcasses, and flies west. Neither Sunny nor Nephis knows what it is.

After a rest and a hearty meal, Sunny realizes that the clarity he gained while dying has never left him, and that he thinks faster and more clearly and acts without hesitation. Later, he sits beside Nephis and thanks her for saving his life twice, and she says that they are allies. When he asks if her Flaw is the pain she feels when using her Ability, she says it feels like burning alive. When he says he is sorry, she answers, 'It's just pain,' which strikes him as the saddest thing he has ever heard.

Sunny checks on his Echo in his Sea of Soul, where it is regenerating inside a cocoon of light, though its lost pincer will not grow back for a while. His Shadow Fragments are now 28 of 1000, since the Echo's killing blow counted as his, and he received four for the centurion's two awakened cores. The soul shards went to Nephis under their agreement, and she consumed one and gave the other to Cassie. He reflects that dormant humans were never meant to fight awakened creatures, and that the Puppeteer's Shroud, which he had hoped would let him hunt weak monsters safely, is just a minimum requirement for survival here.

He reads the description of the Starlight Legion Armor: 'Born in the all-consuming darkness, seven valiant heroes made an oath to return light to the cursed land. Time has erased their names and their faces, but the memory of the defiant oath still remains.' He thinks that Teacher Julius would have loved it. He tells Nephis he has a present and, when she shows no curiosity, takes her hand and transfers the Memory to her.

When she summons it, a black skintight bodysuit forms, followed by white plate armor, greaves, pauldrons, and a breastplate engraved with seven stars identical to those on the headless statue, and a helmet with a white plume. She spins her sword to test it, smiles widely, and says, 'Much better.' Sunny is relieved that she is dressed properly now, and also that he will no longer be distracted.

Back at camp, Nephis tells Cassie that she has found something decent to wear, and Cassie notices that the sound of her footsteps has changed. Nephis lets her touch the white metal. With all three armored, Sunny thinks they finally look like a real Awakened cohort, with delicate Cassie looking like a princess, Nephis like her knight, and himself more like a servant.

Cassie sits beside him and says Nephis told her he nearly died. He shrugs it off, and she apologizes for being useless, saying that she has to be led to walk and fed to eat, and cannot do anything in return. Sunny tells her about his First Nightmare, how his Aspect was described as a useless wretch with no worthwhile skills, yet turned out to be what guided him through alive. He says luck is half circumstance and half your ability to grasp it, and that the Spell takes with one hand and gives with the other. Her Flaw is the most debilitating he has seen, so the power on its other side must be extraordinary, and one day she will be embarrassed to remember how naive she was. She asks if he really believes it, and he says he is the most honest person in two worlds. After a long silence, Cassie says in a low voice that she has had more visions than she has told them about.

chapters.chapter_title: Chapter 56: The Heaviest Thing in the World
chapters.chapter_summary:
Sunny asks why she didn't tell them about the other visions. Cassie says that knowledge can be as heavy as the heaviest thing in the world, and that she fears telling them could cause the things she saw to come true. Sunny knows he should want to know if something terrible is going to happen, but he also sees the danger that preparing for it could cause it, so he stays silent.

Cassie asks him to promise that he will take care of Neph, no matter what. When the Flaw pushes for a truthful reply, he says that he cannot, because he can barely take care of himself and does not yet trust Nephis enough to promise that. He could have misled Cassie with a yes, but strangely does not want to deceive her. She sighs, says 'That's fair,' summons her staff, and walks away, leaving him uneasy.

Trying to distract himself, Sunny assembles clues about the Forgotten Shore, as the Azure Blade's description calls it. The seven heroes of the Starlight Legion whose names are lost, the statue of a headless knight with seven stars, the carapace monsters described in the Echo as 'cursed soldiers of the fallen legion,' and the Starlight Legion Armor dropped by a centurion all seem to fit together, and he wonders if the fallen legion was cursed into becoming the carapace monsters, and if that curse is still active. He also wonders if the seven severed heads guarding seven locks in Cassie's vision might include the statue's missing head. He concludes that he has too little information, and the word 'future' makes him frown.

In the evening, Sunny practices with the sword under Nephis's eye and feels the difference from his new clarity. He asks if the sword is a good weapon for him, and she answers that it depends on his goals, but that the sword is the king of weapons because of its adaptability, like natural selection favoring the most adaptable species rather than the strongest. A spear is better against long reach, a war hammer against armor, and a mace is easier to maintain, but a sword can pierce, cut, and bash at many ranges, and every part of it can be used. She ends with, 'It doesn't matter that much what's in your hands. You are the weapon.' She is much more eloquent when she talks about things she is confident in.
