Watching the sunset, Sunny voices his doubts about reaching the castle. Nephis says yes, they will, and when he asks why she is so sure, she answers, 'If that is our will, who dares to stop us?'

That night scavengers try to climb the cliffs, and Sunny and Nephis push them off, bringing his fragments to 32. They spend another day resting, since the Echo is still recovering. Nephis meditates with what seems to be a faint white glow behind her eyelids, and Sunny suspects she is training herself to endure her Flaw. Cassie seems cheerful as usual but more resolute. The next morning they eat the last of the centurion's meat and begin to climb down to continue west.

Two weeks later, Sunny sits on a dead scavenger, wiping blue blood from his face as the Spell announces another stronger shadow. They have just killed a Carapace Centurion that had been tracking them for days. They lured it into a narrow passage, and the noise drew in scavengers and centipede-like creatures at war with the carapace legion, and Sunny and Nephis used that animosity to come out as the only victors. The Echo has regrown its pincer and is now gorging on the centurion's corpse.

Since leaving the cliffs, they have moved west from one high point to the next, scouting every route in advance to avoid another storm, with Cassie riding the Echo. After the centurion fight showed them how much stronger they must become, they now hunt scavengers, targeting isolated ones or groups of no more than three. In the Starlight Legion Armor, Nephis is a menace, and her power grows with each soul shard she absorbs. Sunny gains shadow fragments at about the same rate, though he cannot take every kill, and he does not have to share them with Cassie. He is also improving by learning sword work from her and fighting every day, and through experience and clarity.

But the biggest improvement comes from teamwork, as they have developed a wordless coordination that makes it as if their numbers doubled. Even Cassie is growing stronger, learning to function without sight less than two months after losing it, and caring for her is becoming less of a burden. Reaching the castle begins to feel possible.

chapters.chapter_title: Chapter 59: Shadow of the Crimson Spire
chapters.chapter_summary:
After the fight, Sunny whistles to tell Cassie it is safe, and guides her to the Echo, telling her about the six centipede monsters and some scavengers they let fight each other before finishing the survivors. He explains that the labyrinth holds other horrors, including worm colonies, flesh-eating flowers with strangling vines, and tentacles that drag scavengers into crevices, all of at least Awakened rank. The carapace legion seems to dominate this region, which is better than facing many different threats. The centipede monsters are over three meters long, fast, and secrete a corrosive black oil by mixing two sacks. Their chitin is weak against a sword, though. They collected eleven soul shards, their biggest haul so far, but no Memory for two weeks, which makes Sunny complain about the Spell. He scolds the Echo for eating half the centurion, a habit that Cassie defends affectionately by calling it a 'he.'

Nephis insists on saving the centipede oil, which is flammable. Deciding to push on to the Bone Ridge, they see the sun is high and the way is mostly scouted. As they approach, Sunny feels the same unease that has bothered him every evening since leaving the cliffs, growing stronger the farther west they go. Cassie guesses that it must be related to his shadow sense, and he realizes that at sunset a vast, distant shadow sweeps through the labyrinth. Cassie says it is the shadow of the Crimson Spire.

Cassie says that in her dream, the Spire was as tall as a mountain, visible from the castle walls, and that at sunset its shadow stretches east over the castle. The feeling she had looking at it was like what Sunny describes, but stronger. Sunny wonders if the labyrinth's crimson material, which is not really coral, is the same as the Spire's, and Cassie suggests it might be the other way around. He realizes that since the castle lies between them and the Spire, the shadow works as a compass for him.

The Bone Ridge is a skeleton of a gigantic sea monster on a mound of coral, one of many leviathan skeletons in the labyrinth. Sunny sees the coral as ancient solidified blood growing out of bones. They enter through its cracked skull and walk up the hollow spine, which is as wide as a highway. Nothing is inside, and they reach the top as the sun sets and the sea returns.

Sunny's Shadow Fragments are 96 of 1000, up from twelve, but he is still far weaker than the weakest creatures here, and his Shadow Core cannot awaken until he returns to the real world. After the girls wash, he uses the water bottle to clean himself and removes the Shroud. They eat meat seasoned with sea salt, and Sunny takes first watch while practicing sword forms. He notices that the black water in the spine is perfectly flat and still, like a mirror made of darkness. He feels an urge to look at his reflection, but is terrified of what might look back, and does not.

Sunny wakes uneasy, still shaken by the dark mirror of the night before, and reflects that shadow and true darkness are not the same thing. Nephis, who watched the last part of the night, opens her eyes with a faint white afterglow in them. For the past two weeks she has been training harder than he has, though not at swordsmanship. She has been learning to behave like a normal human, studying how Cassie talks and then awkwardly imitating her. Today her polite smile looks nearly natural. He also knows that her meditation is really her enduring the agony of her Flaw to learn to control her Ability, and the thought makes his heart ache, which he guesses is compassion.

After breakfast, he boosts Nephis up through a gap in the spine, and she lowers the rope. From the top, they see the crimson labyrinth turn grey and dead in the west, with brittle, crumbling coral that gives way to a sea of ash-colored sand. In the distance, there is a huge hill like a barrow, topped by a giant tree with black bark and blood-red leaves, large enough to shade the entire island. Something beneath it glints like a mirror, which unsettles Sunny. Nephis says that this is the only way west.

They leave the Bone Ridge and enter the wasteland, expecting an ambush. They find no monsters at all, which makes Sunny more nervous. At the edge, where the walls give way to open sand between them and the hill, he asks if she is sure, and she says, 'Let's go.'

In the open wasteland, Sunny feels exposed and mildly agoraphobic, since the labyrinth's walls had been protective and his shadow scouting no longer works the same way. Nothing is moving, and neither his shadow nor Cassie's hearing detects anything. Nephis redirects them toward one of the low knolls scattered across the flat ground. At noon, as she is about to touch it, Sunny's shadow spots a movement back at the labyrinth's edge and he whispers for everyone to hide. He dismisses the Echo, catches Cassie as she falls, and pulls them all down behind the knoll.

A carapace centurion walks out of the labyrinth, and Sunny knows that they could not beat it in a straight fight. It is headed for the Ashen Barrow, and they stay pressed together against the knoll, which makes Sunny very aware of Cassie's body. In its scythes, the centurion carries a gleaming transcendent soul shard, like those the two monsters took from the shark's carcass. It passes the knoll without noticing them.

Sunny's shadow follows it to the foot of the hill, where the centurion stops as though at an invisible line, puts down the shard, backs away, and kneels, lowering its scythes. Sunny struggles to believe it. Meanwhile his shadow notices the bright glimmer he saw from the leviathan's spine, now rising from the shade of the tree and descending the slope toward the kneeling centurion. When he finally sees what is making it, he goes cold.

The glimmer comes from an enormous monster as large as a house, descending the hill on eight pillar-like legs. It is built like a scavenger or centurion, but its carapace is polished chrome-like metal instead of chitin, covered in long spikes and engraved with what look like seven stars on its chest. It has four arms, two with pincers and two with scythes, and a horned, almost human face. It is the next step beyond a centurion, something like a general. The centurion cowers under its gaze. The Carapace Demon picks up the soul shard and returns to the shade of the tree.

Sunny cannot resist sending his shadow after it. Under the great tree, it sees the demon drop the shard, reach up with a pincer, gently pick a ripe fruit, and bite into it, which leaves Sunny wondering if the monster is vegetarian. His shadow then hurries to catch up with the centurion as it returns to the labyrinth. Sunny finally tells the girls it is safe to come out and says they must go back, and Nephis trusts him enough not to question it. Before leaving, he brushes the sand off the knoll and finds black bark, so it is a tree root, and the ash sea is the tree's doing.

Back inside the Bone Ridge, he describes the demon, whose metal armor has no visible gaps, with four huge arms and a face more sentient than anything else they have faced, and says it must have three cores, an awakened demon, or even a devil. He says they should avoid it at all costs. Nephis stares at him until he guesses that she wants to kill it.

Sunny protests that the Carapace Demon is out of their league. Cassie points out that he said much the same thing before they attacked the first centurion, and Nephis adds, 'You survived, didn't you?' Cassie scolds her and Nephis awkwardly rephrases. Sunny continues to object out of principle, noting that it is too tall to reach, but privately senses that the fight is inevitable. He reflects that Nephis seems driven by demons of her own, pursuing a goal that matters more to her than her own life, and he cannot understand why she is more determined to reach the castle than he is. When he asks if they can avoid the barrow, she says that it is the only way west.

He accepts this, but says they cannot defeat it in a fight. Then, with a dark smile, he says that does not mean they cannot kill it. When Nephis asks if he has a plan, he says not yet, but he knows that unlike scavengers and centurions, the demon is intelligent, which means it can be deceived.

They spend the night in the leviathan's spine. Sunny considers staying there for weeks to grow stronger, then decides that every extra day on the Forgotten Shore risks fatal bad luck, and the best chance is to face the demon soon. He lies awake working on an idea, falls asleep near morning, and is woken half an hour later by Cassie, who is pale and says she had another vision, this time about the Carapace Demon.

Cassie says her vision was of the past. She saw the Ashen Barrow at night in a raging storm, with the demon standing in it like a fortress of steel while lightning played between his spikes, unaffected. A last bolt hit the ground and ignited the fallen leaves, and the island burned like a beacon. Sunny recalls that the girls' fire on the night of the first light attracted monsters from the dark sea. Then the sea surged, and a gigantic mass of bones, rotten flesh, black seaweed, tentacles, and thousands of eyes crawled up the slope toward the great tree. It seemed slow and weakened outside the water. The demon attacked it at once, as if enraged.

Cassie did not see the battle, only its end. At dawn the demon crawled back under the tree, missing legs, scythes cracked, and a fracture in his chest armor exposing his beating heart. He healed over time, and his limbs regrew, but the chest fracture was the last to heal and did not close completely, so a weakness remains hidden in his armor.

Nephis says that means the demon is not impenetrable, and asks Sunny how his plan is going. He says it is going well, and Cassie's vision gave him inspiration. They will have to deceive the demon with a trojan horse. The next day they return to the site where they lured the centurion, and Sunny is pleased to find the centurion's empty carapace, cleaned of flesh and in perfect condition.

chapters.chapter_title: Chapter 66: First Part of the Plan
chapters.chapter_summary:
Near evening, a lopsided, drunkenly staggering carapace centurion walks out of the dead labyrinth into the wasteland. It is actually the Echo hiding under the empty carapace of the dead centurion, with Sunny's shadow riding beneath it, facepalming when a scythe falls off. It crosses toward the Ashen Barrow and slumps down at its base with no tribute. The Carapace Demon rises, descends the slope and, without hesitation or suspicion, instantly slices the disguise in half to reveal only emptiness.

On the other side of the hill, Sunny, running with Cassie on his back, swears. The plan was for the Echo to lure the demon away while the three circled the hill, hid beneath the sand, then raced up to climb the great tree before Sunny dismissed the Echo. The demon's rapid attack has wrecked the timing. With no other option, Sunny orders the Echo to attack and stall. It tries to dive under the demon's body as Nephis once did against the first centurion, but the demon swats it away and nearly cracks its shell. Nephis puts down the rucksack she carries and starts climbing the trunk.

The Echo gets up and charges again, accompanied by Sunny's human shadow and its own shadow. The demon calmly cuts off both of its arms, lifts it, and tears it in two. In his mind, Sunny hears the Spell announce that his Echo has been destroyed.

Sunny stumbles at the news that his Echo is dead, and feels its connection vanish, one of the spheres of light in his Sea of Soul fading. He mourns, since he had come to like the mindless, loyal scavenger, but there is no time. The demon stands over the corpse as it dissolves into light and leaves nothing, revealing Sunny's shadow, which was hiding in the Echo's larger shadow. The demon impales it with a scythe, to no effect, but then turns to look at the top of the hill, realizing that it has been tricked, and charges up the slope with frightening speed.

At the tree, Sunny helps Cassie off his back and gives her Nephis's rucksack to hold carefully. Nephis is already on a high branch and drops the golden rope. Before sending Cassie up, he has her summon her wooden staff and guides her to raise a gale that blows the leaves and sand off a large patch of the island, wiping out their tracks. His shadow overtakes the demon and rejoins him. Nephis hauls Cassie up, then Sunny climbs quickly, and Nephis dismisses the golden rope just as the demon arrives.

The three crouch on the wide branch while the demon searches below, looks up without seeing them, and finds no footprints under the tree. At the edge of the cleared area, he finds the two sets of tracks and charges down toward the wasteland. As the rumble of the returning sea announces sunset, he gives up and trudges back to the top of his barrow.

The three wait silently on the branch for night to fall, with the demon sometimes passing below. Sunny cannot recover from losing the Echo, and Cassie squeezes his hand, which comforts him more than he would admit. After dark, he says, 'Let's begin.' From the rucksack, he removes two clay jars he made himself, containing the two separate components of the centipede oil, which become corrosive and flammable when mixed. He also takes out a bone-and-seaweed torch and places it in Nephis's hand. She closes her eyes, white light ignites beneath her eyelids, and fire bursts from her hands onto the torch, which she holds above her head like a lonely star in the dark.

Sunny screams, 'HEY, ASSHOLE! COME GET ME IF YOU DARE!' at the demon, taunting it as a pile of scrap and a fat lobster. The demon charges to the tree, too short to reach their branch. Sunny drops the jars, and the demon slices them but is covered in the mixing oil, which turns out to do nothing to its alloy armor. Nephis, who expected that, throws the torch, and the demon bursts into flames. Sunny never expected the fire to hurt it. The point is that the burning demon becomes a bright beacon in the dark, calling every monster of the dark sea.

The burning demon roars in fury, and Sunny admits that the real plan was always to let the monsters of the dark sea do the killing. The demon considers climbing the tree, then instead rolls on the ground to try to put out the flames. Then Nephis turns toward the sea, and Sunny senses a pressure in the air as the world feels subtly wrong. A cold wall of fog rises above the water and creeps onto the island against the wind, with a figure inside it. The demon stops and faces it with grim resignation, then bloodlust.

Cassie covers Sunny's eyes and whispers, 'Don't look.' The fog touches him, and her voice multiplies and distorts from all directions into a scream. When it stops, her voice says, 'Open your eyes,' but it comes from the wrong direction, without breath, and from too low to be hers. When the voice repeats, 'OPEN YOUR EYES!' he keeps them shut. After an eternity it withdraws. Beneath them, the demon clashes his scythes, which pushes the fog away in a sphere of clean air, and the island shakes as he fights the horror. Sunny grabs his companions and they hold on.

At dawn, the fight is over. The island is torn up as if shelled. The Carapace Demon limps back from the edge, bleeding, missing two arms, most of his rear legs, and an eye, his carapace cracked all over, but his vital armor plates are intact. Sunny asks what they do, and Nephis summons her sword and says, 'Finish him off.'

Sunny accepts that they have to fight it themselves, since his bag of tricks is empty, and asks how they will deal with the armor. Nephis says she will break through if he can create an opening. As she ties the rope to the branch, Sunny tries to cheer up Cassie by promising to cook her a demon steak once they have the meat, and she gives him a real smile and accepts it as a promise.

On the ground, the crippled demon, missing an eye, with shattered horns and a broken front leg, is still radiating intelligence and bloodlust toward the two who caused his state. Sunny warns Nephis that he is very fast, and they close in from opposite sides, Sunny on the side with the scythe and eye, Nephis on the side of the pincer. He plans to take the brunt of the attacks while she delivers the lethal blow. Sunny fakes a stumble to bait the scythe, which hits only sand, then runs to the demon's legs and slashes, but the Azure Blade bounces off the polished armor. On the other side, Nephis cuts deep through a crack in the armor of the injured front leg, and it buckles, but the demon braces with his scythe in the ground and does not fall.

Sunny had hoped to avoid what comes next. He holds his breath and ducks beneath the demon's steel abdomen.

With the demon bracing on his scythe, Sunny has a second of safety and dives under the creature's belly. Under thick shadow and tons of metal, he stays focused and watches the leg joints for the slightest shift. When he sees it, he sprints sideways, and the demon throws his whole body down to crush him. Sunny dives out with centimeters to spare as the massive body hits the ground and shakes the island. The risk was deliberate, since the demon has to be forced to the ground in reach of their blades. Now he is lying on his abdomen, with his torso and vital organs in range of Nephis's sword.

But the scythe comes at once, and Sunny escapes it with an awkward high somersault. He moves in front of the demon to draw its attention away from Nephis, but misjudges the demon's reaction time and has no time to dodge a horizontal thrust. Unlike the first centurion fight, he blocks it with the Azure Blade, one hand on the hilt and the other gripping the blade's tip, angled to deflect most of the force. His shadow keeps his hands from breaking. The sword shatters near the crossguard, and the Spell begins announcing the loss of his Memory as he is thrown back across the sand.

He lands about two dozen meters from the trunk of the great tree, and sees the demon starting to turn toward Nephis. As the remains of the sword begin to glow, he throws them at the tree trunk instead. The demon freezes for a moment, following the sparks, which gives Nephis exactly what she needs.

Nephis lunges the instant the demon is distracted, as she has been waiting for this moment since the battle began. As she runs, the white flame under her skin flows out of her hands into the hilt and then the blade, turning her sword into a blade of incandescent white light that seems able to reduce anything to ash. Sunny understands that this is what she meant when she said her Ability could be used to heal, and that her secret agony was training to endure the pain of using it in battle. The demon moves his scythe and pincer to stop her, but she is a fraction faster.

She leaps and drives the sword into the demon's chest, precisely at the spot where Cassie's vision showed the armor never fully healed. The blade pierces the metal and goes into the heart, burning everything inside and boiling the blood. The demon staggers, his arms rising as if to embrace her, then falling. As he dies, his remaining eye looks at the great tree and then at Sunny, with something that looks like relief. The intelligence leaves his gaze.

Nephis removes her helmet, pale and exhausted, and lies on her back. The whole fight lasted less than a minute. Sunny lies down too, hardly believing they won, then remembers that Cassie is still waiting in the branches and shouts, 'One demon steak, coming right up!'

A few minutes later, Cassie climbs down the rope on her own, quickly and carefully, and finds Sunny by his voice. He is lying on the ground and says it is comfortable, which worries her until he says he is only bruised and Nephis is fine. She asks if they really killed the demon, and he tells her he is very dead. Eventually they gather in a circle by the corpse, passing the water bottle. Nephis tries to smile politely and Sunny scores it 3.6 out of ten. He describes the fight, and Cassie is amazed that two Sleepers killed an awakened demon, and Nephis insists that it was three, since without Cassie's vision they would have failed.

When Sunny offers to make the demon steak he promised, Cassie hesitates. It seems wrong to eat an intelligent creature, even an evil one. Sunny realizes that the demon had thoughts, pride, and valor, and agrees she may be right. Cassie then suggests eating the fruits of the great tree instead, and Sunny is amazed. He argues the tree is suspicious, since it is probably the reason the coral around it is dead, and cannot be trusted. Cassie finds him paranoid and says the tree is a wonderful example of life prevailing. This is unlike her, and unsettles him, but Nephis agrees with Sunny and says the fruits are too risky.

Nephis then asks about the Echo and his sword, and he says both are lost. Nephis says that he is in luck, because she received a Memory from the Carapace Demon, a weapon.

Sunny forgets about the Azure Blade immediately, since a Memory from an awakened demon is a tier-three Awakened Memory, two tiers above the Azure Blade. Nephis takes his hand and transfers it, and the Spell announces that he has received the Midnight Shard. Its description reads, 'Forged from the shard of a fallen star, this stalwart blade is firm and unyielding. It favors those who are willing to fight to the last drop of blood and knows no surrender.' It is a plain, slightly curved single-edged sword, seventy to eighty centimeters long, with a black wooden hilt and a round crossguard, made from the same bright metal as the demon's armor. Holding it, he senses an unbreakable will, and also a deep well of power just out of reach that he might unlock by earning the sword's favor. Nephis tells him it is technically a tachi.

He asks if she wants to keep it for herself, since she killed the demon, and she says her own sword suits her. Sunny notes that she refuses an upgrade, which suggests her silver sword is better than a tier-three weapon, and wonders again how she got her True Name.

Fearing that the winged creature will come for the demon's corpse, they move to the far side of the great tree and sleep. This time Sunny has a dream, which should not be possible in the Dream Realm.

Sunny wakes to his shadow's urgent alarm, pointing upward, and tries to recall the dream he had. Fragments of it come back: Cassie gripped him by the shoulders, terrified, begging him to remember that it is five, repeating, 'Five! It's five! You have to remember!' Then the shadow waves him toward the threat in the sky, and Sunny forgets the dream and that it was strange at all, which he does not notice. He did not notice, either, that it may not be the first thing he has forgotten at the Barrow.

He goes to the eastern slope and sees a black dot circling above the island, probably one of the creatures that ate the centurion. Over the following hours, it is joined by two others of the same breed, white-bodied and black-feathered, each strong enough to wipe out their group. They circle and sometimes approach, but never land in the shade of the tree, as if reluctant. The three hide and watch, hungry, and Nephis jokes about grilled chicken, which stuns Sunny. At sunset the creatures fly west in a loose wedge.

When Cassie says that waiting was five times worse than hiding at the cliffs, Sunny flinches without knowing why, then dismisses it. They go to the western edge of the island, hoping to see the castle. Nephis climbs the rampart first and goes rigid, with a resentful look on her face. Sunny looks west, and begins cursing inwardly.

Beyond the western edge, the land does not continue as flat wasteland. It slopes steadily down into an enormous crater hundreds of kilometers across, with the great tree's roots like blades of grass against its walls. There are no more high places to the west, and the only way forward is down into the reach of the dark sea. Their journey west appears to be over. At sunset, the dark sea rushes in from beyond the horizon, fills the crater, and overflows, flooding the wasteland and labyrinth. Sunny says that they have found the source of the dark sea, and Nephis says to head back.

Cassie is stunned that this contradicts her vision of reaching the castle and keeps asking Sunny if he is sure there is nothing higher. Nephis says they will think of something tomorrow, and that worst case, they will have to circle the crater, which would take months and is almost certainly deadly. As Sunny falls asleep, he vaguely thinks about the odd dream, but cannot recall it.

The next morning they are hungry and gloomy. Nephis says she will climb the great tree to look for anything missed from the height and leaves him with Cassie. Sunny trains with the Midnight Shard for an hour, then removes the three soul shards from the demon's corpse. He also searches for the transcendent soul shard that the demon dropped on the sand, but cannot find it. When he returns, he sees Nephis and Cassie sitting with red-stained lips, eating the fruits of the great tree.

Nephis and Cassie are eating the black-skinned, ruby-fleshed fruits, juice smeared over their hands and chins. Sunny shouts at them, and they are confused. When he says they agreed to avoid the fruits, Nephis asks, 'Did we? ...Why?' and Sunny realizes that he has no idea why, as his memory is blank. Hunger clouds his thinking, and Cassie suggests he is only upset they started without him, and points to a third fruit that Nephis brought for him. He bites in and finds it the most delicious thing he has ever tasted. He feels that something is wrong and notices his shadow refusing to mimic his movement, as if it is reluctant to touch the fruit. He briefly thinks of the name Soul Tree, and nearly remembers something important, but is distracted by the Spell announcing that his shadow has grown stronger.

Nephis says that she has absorbed a point of soul essence, and Cassie says she got hers a few bites ago. Sunny checks and sees that his Shadow Fragments are 97 of 1000, a gain from eating alone. The demon, he concludes, was fixated on the fruits for this reason, and he forgets his unease and eats on.

That evening they move camp between the tree's roots. With no way west, they decide to take a few days' vacation on the safe island. The only thing that nags him is a last thought, before falling asleep, that it is a shame no one will be here to serve the tree, feed it, and spread its seeds.

Sunny wakes under the scarlet crown of the Soul Tree feeling more peaceful than he has in a long time. Nephis asks if he remembers why no one kept watch the night before, and he can't, and neither does she seem to care for long. Cassie declares them to be on vacation and forbids him from planning, plotting, or scheming. He feels that he is forgetting something and asks Nephis why she climbed the tree the day before, and she only says that it was probably to get the fruits.

A few days pass in idleness. They sleep until noon, eat the fruits, talk, and play games. Sunny, a loner for most of his life, relishes the privacy after weeks of constant company. All three are increasingly absentminded, and he sometimes catches himself struggling to remember his past life or noticing how strange things are, but the thought slips away. His memory becomes hazier, and he becomes convinced that the Soul Tree is beautiful, benevolent, and generous, protecting them and nourishing their bodies and cores.

Only Nephis grows gloomy. She spends her time at the western edge, staring, and her hair seems to be growing longer. When Sunny approaches, with a painful headache, she asks if they should not continue west, and cannot say why, except that she feels she has to do something very important. Sunny has no answer, but he thinks he knows how to help her feel better. He will find her an especially juicy fruit.

It is already dark when Sunny returns to the camp. Cassie sleeps with a peaceful smile and has not had a terrible vision in a long time. Nephis has not returned from the western edge, close to the black water. Sunny reflects that he has picked the lowest branches clean, and that the ripest fruits give one or two shadow fragments each, while smaller ones give one or none. He does not think to check his count of fragments, which would have horrified him.

Deciding to find a special fruit for Nephis without waiting until morning, he climbs the tree in the dark. Without sunlight the crown looks eerie and still, and the rustling of the leaves sounds like thousands of souls screaming in agony. He shakes off the thought and apologizes to the tree. A strange thought about its ravenous hunger and desire to devour slips in, and then he cannot remember what he was thinking.

He climbs higher than he has ever been, through a maze of branches, past fruits that are ripe but not special, until the branches are thin and barely hold his weight. In his night vision, where color is muted, he notices a cluster of branches bent downward, hidden by an almost impenetrable wall of leaves. Using the shadow to enhance his strength, he forces his way through, and sees a giant bird's nest woven from the tree's branches in a pocket between the leaves.

The nest is spherical, built of onyx branches as thick as a man's arm, with an entrance large enough for a small truck. It looks ancient and abandoned, with a feeling of desolation. Sunny's usual caution is overridden by curiosity and by his belief that anything connected to the Soul Tree must be safe. He jumps in and lands on a thick bed of brittle white spiderwebs. In the center is a giant, ancient-looking egg, as tall as he is, stone grey with swirling cloud-like patterns. He is thrilled by the discovery. When he touches it, it is warm, and he feels a pull on his core as if it is trying to steal his life force. It fails, he realizes, because he alone in two worlds has no soul core, only a Shadow Core.

He understands that this must be the unhatched spawn of a powerful Nightmare Creature, and considers that anyone who feeds it enough soul essence could hatch it. His decisions lately have been strange, and he vaguely worries that his thinking is reduced, but decides that a true explorer has to kill whatever he discovers. The Midnight Shard bounces off, leaving a shallow scratch, so he wraps the blade in his shadow, which turns it black and lusterless and gives it a cold aura, and slices down. Cracks run through the egg, a flash of crimson light shows and goes out, and black fluid pours onto the webs. The Spell announces that he has slain a Great Devil, a Vile Thieving Bird's Spawn, that his shadow grows stronger, and that he has received a Memory.

Sunny realizes what he has just killed. A Great Devil has four souls cores of the Great rank, which would equal Supreme rank for humans. He might have killed one of the most powerful Nightmare Creatures ever slain by a human, and he was only able to because the egg was unborn, weakened by thousands of years of neglect, and he alone is partly immune to its life-draining powers. He expects sixty-four shadow fragments, based on how much each core is worth, and when he checks his count, it says 196 of 1000. He frowns that this is thirty-six more than he should have, since he had 96 before the island, and tries to work out where they came from, but his thoughts slip away and he gives up.

He checks the Memory he received from the Great Devil, the Drop of Ichor, whose rank and type are listed as unknown. The description says that the loathsome Thieving Bird, enamored of Weaver's beautiful eyes, stole one on a starless night, looked into it in flight, saw the reflection of something unknown frozen in Weaver's pupil, went mad, and dropped the eye, keeping only one drop of golden ichor. Some words are untranslatable and looking at the runes makes him dizzy. When he summons the Memory, a golden drop hangs in the air and the Spell asks, almost excitedly, if he wishes to consume it.

He considers just putting it back, but cannot let go of an opportunity from a Great Devil and says yes. The drop splits into two streams that flow into his eyes. After a pause, he screams in terrible pain.

Sunny collapses onto the webs, convulsing in agony, and feels his body torn apart and reassembled over and over, with his eyes feeling like white-hot rods. The scratches he makes on his face vanish at once, and soon his voice is gone. The process is the opposite of his gentle rebirth after the First Nightmare, violent and unnatural. After an eternity it subsides. The Spell announces that he has acquired a new Attribute and that one of his Attributes is ready to evolve.

When he finally dares to look, he finds that he is still human, with no change in strength. But his vision is deeper than before, and he notices a faint golden shine in a drop of blood from a scratch that has not healed. Glancing at the Puppeteer's Shroud, he suddenly sees five glowing embers beneath the fabric, each one a nexus of countless diamond strings. He senses the purpose behind the pattern, as though it is his innate ability.

In his Sea of Soul, he looks to the periphery as he always does, and for the first time he sees what is there, motionless black figures standing at the edge of the light. They are the shadows of everything he has killed, including the broad-shouldered slave twisted into a larva host, Mountain King, the cruel slaver, scavengers, a centurion, centipedes, worms, and man-eating flowers. They seem to be staring at him.

The shadows do nothing, and Sunny concludes that they are manifestations of his Aspect and are harmless, probably always present but now visible because of his changed eyes. He studies his Memories, which appear differently now. The Puppeteer's Shroud shows five glowing nexuses, matching a tier-five Memory from a five-core tyrant, and its description now includes the tier and two enchantments, [Enhanced Durability] and [Doubtless], the latter giving a small protection against mind attacks. The Silver Bell has one spark, tier one dormant, and its enchantment extends how far the ringing carries. The Midnight Shard is tier III with the enchantment [Unbroken], making it durable beyond reason and enhancing the wielder when they are close to death, but only if they refuse to surrender, which means it is useful only when he is already in trouble.

When he looks at his Attributes, he sees [Fated], [Mark of Divinity], [Child of Shadows], and the new [Blood Weave], and realizes something is wrong. He feels uneasy, tied to the number five, and thinks there should be five Attributes but can read only four. Every time he looks at the fifth, he is distracted and forgets. Biting his lip to clear his mind, he shouts, 'Five! It's five! There's five of them, damn it!' A veil lifts from his mind, and he remembers that the dream was real: Cassie begging him to remember the number five.

Sunny remembers what really happened on the day they killed the Carapace Demon. After the three fell asleep, an hour or two later Cassie shook him awake in terror, saying, 'You have to stop it! You are the only one who can!' He summoned the Midnight Shard and Nephis summoned her sword, but there was no enemy. Cassie told him that she would forget soon, and that they all would, but that he must remember, begging him, 'Five! It's five!' She explained that the more complex a thought, the harder it would be to hold on to, so she could only give him the simplest word, which might change things when the right time came. He promised to remember.

By the time he asked her to explain, she was confused and asked if something had happened. Sunny and Nephis could not remember why they had their swords out. Cassie then recalled a vision, a mountain of corpses piled into a bloodsoaked hill with a tiny black seed floating in a pool of blood at its top, which she thought was the past, and then a future in which they were doing something she could not bring herself to say. A moment later, she forgot what she was saying, and so did Sunny. Nephis told them to go back to sleep, and Sunny did.

Hours later, when his shadow noticed the winged creature, the memory seemed like a dream. But the seed Cassie planted survived deep in his subconscious, and now that it has bloomed, he can remember everything.

chapters.chapter_title: Chapter 85: One Step at a Time
chapters.chapter_summary:
Sitting in the nest, Sunny works through what he now knows. Since they came to the Ashen Barrow their minds have been affected, making them forgetful and distractible, and the fruit's gain of shadow fragments suggests that nearly a month has passed. He has gaps in his memory, such as how they got here or where they were going. He sets himself steps: first, resist forgetting, and second, find out why he alone could remember. The answer is the Puppeteer's Shroud's [Doubtless] enchantment, which gave him some resistance to mind attacks. That is why he was the last to eat the fruit and why Cassie chose him. This means the culprit is the Soul Tree, a colossal, ancient Nightmare Creature of unimaginable power, which explains why even other monsters avoid the island, and why the coral around it is dead. He considers setting it on fire, but it would take a volcano.

He tries again to read the description of the hidden fifth Attribute, with no success. He then checks the Mark of Divinity, which is ready to evolve, and he says yes. It becomes [Spark of Divinity]: 'Every fire starts from a spark. Somewhere deep within your soul, a radiant spark shines with divine light.' He thinks Weaver may be one of the Unknown rather than a god, and that his new sight comes from the ichor. The Blood Weave reads, 'You have inherited a part of Weaver's forbidden lineage. Your blood has been altered and embued with odd tenacity.'

At dawn he climbs down without any fruit and wakes Cassie, mirroring how she once woke him, and asks her to look at his Attributes.

Throughout the climb down, Sunny bites his hands to clear his mind, and he notices that Blood Weave makes the wounds scab quickly and gives him more energy and endurance. His plan is to use Cassie's Aspect Ability, which comes from her Aspect rather than the Spell's runes and so should not be affected by the enthrallment, and her affinity to revelations makes her the best chance to read the hidden Attribute. He wakes her and asks her to look. She reads, 'Fated, Child of Shadows, Spark of Divinity… wait, wasn't it 'mark' of divinity?' and yawns, then notices Blood Weave and gets distracted when he says it came from an egg.

His heart racing, he waits as she says, 'The last one is Enthralled. Wait… where did this…' He urges her to read the description, and she says, 'You've been mesmerized by the ancient fiend, Soul Devouring Tree, and are being turned into its thrall. Once the process is complete, there will be no escape.' As soon as he hears it, the chains fall from his mind and his memories return in an avalanche. He realizes how close he came to being obliterated without knowing.

He thanks Cassie, who has already forgotten and is only confused. Her memory and mind are still compromised and getting worse. She yawns, lies down, and falls asleep, blissfully unaware that her days are numbered. Sunny watches her and thinks, 'Over my dead body.'

Sunny finds Nephis at the western edge of the island and, with clearer eyes, sees how she has changed. Her silver hair has grown to cover her ears, her face is thin with dark circles, and she seems to be wasting away. He suspects that her burning determination to reach her goal is strong enough to resist the Soul Tree's enthrallment, but with her memories gone, she is left longing for something she cannot name, and that conflict is what is consuming her.

He tells her everything: the nest, the Spawn, the Drop of Ichor, the new Attribute, the Enthralled Attribute, what the tree is, and how much time has passed. She says only, 'I see,' and he yells at her to behave like a human. She stays quiet, and he notices sparks of white radiance in her eyes, since she has activated her Ability to use pain to stay lucid. When he asks her what to do, she says, 'We need to build a boat.'

She reasons that the Soul Tree's commands included not leaving the island, so its effect must weaken with distance and break if they get far enough. As for why not run on foot, she says it would take many months to circle the crater through the labyrinth without the Echo, and sooner or later they would meet another Soul Tree or something deadlier. A boat with Cassie's staff filling the sail could cover a hundred or two hundred kilometers in one night, more than they have covered in weeks. It is a gamble either way. Sunny feels very cold and small.

Sunny reminds Nephis of the creatures in the dark sea, and she says they are damned either way. She plans to avoid fires and use his eyes to guide them west, and hopes that Cassie's armor helps. When he asks, she explains that it is a tier-six Awakened Memory, and one of its traits is making the wearer less likely to draw an enemy's attention. Then she trembles and says that she is at her limit and her mind is fading, so he should ask what he needs to fast. He asks if she knows how to build a boat, and she nods. He asks how to convince her to leave once her memory is gone, and for a moment her eyes clear with white flame, and she says, 'Aster... Song... Vale. Say those words to me, and I will listen.' She also says to take Cassie and flee if anything happens. Then the light fades and she forgets everything.

When she looks at him, confused, he asks her cheerfully if she knows how to build a boat. Dodging her questions with the finesse his Flaw allows, he convinces her to help. Sunny keeps his mind together by biting his own hand. They plan to build the hull from plates of the dead demon's carapace, tied with the golden rope. The demon's body has not rotted, but its metal is rusting and losing its luster. She points out suitable curved plates, that are each long enough for the whole hull. Sunny suggests using Cassie's cloak as the sail, and she is puzzled about his enthusiasm for the project but agrees. He goes to fetch Cassie.

Sunny has much to do before sunset. He must use pain constantly to prevent himself from forgetting, and his hands and arms are covered with bite marks, which Blood Weave keeps from becoming dangerous. Cassie is in worse shape than either he or Nephis, and he wonders if it is because they have True Names and she does not, since names anchor identity. He guides her to the carcass and sits her where Nephis can see her. Nephis is already stripping plates from the demon's back with her silver sword, which cuts the deteriorated metal easily.

He tells her that he has a project of his own and wants to make a candle, which makes her ask Cassie if he has lost his mind. He cuts out fat from the demon's flesh and spends the rest of the day making the candle and gathering as many fallen leaves as he can, for reasons he does not explain. Because he has convinced the girls that the boat is just a hobby, he alone bears the weight of the enthrallment, and he is exhausted, his head full of molten iron and his vision blurry.

By evening the boat is finished, more than the raft he expected, with a hull of curved plates bristling with spikes and bound with the golden rope, a mast made from the demon's spine and ribs with Cassie's cloak as a sail, and a steering oar from a scythe tip. When Nephis asks what comes next, he finds an invisible barrier in his mind. Biting his palm does not help, so he kneels and brings the pommel of the Midnight Shard down on his ring finger. The pain obliterates the barrier, and he thinks, 'Now we get the hell out of here!'

Nephis is shocked at his self-mutilation. Sunny complains about his broken finger, and brushes off Cassie's question, then asks Nephis to help him drag the boat to the edge of the island. He does not want to reveal the true purpose until the last moment. He tells Cassie to wait and promises to come get her, and apologizes to her silently. The two drag the spiked boat across the island with the golden rope around his chest while the sun sinks and a rumble announces that the dark sea is awakening. The alloy of the hull is the same lightweight metal as the Midnight Shard, which is said to come from a fallen star. At the edge, he tells Nephis not to go anywhere until he returns with Cassie, and she shrugs.

He goes back to Cassie, who asks only for fruit. When he says that he has none, she repeats it like a broken doll. He tries to misdirect her, but because of his exhaustion, his Flaw slips, and he answers that he will not take her to the fruits and that he wants to take her away from the cursed island. She refuses and shouts that the island is their home. Sunny shouts back that the tree is evil and then, 'Because it's five! Remember?!' She resists, but he lifts her and runs to the boat as she pummels him with surprisingly strong blows and screams for Nephis.

At the shore, Nephis rises, summons her silver sword, and demands an explanation in a calm voice. Sunny remembers that she, too, is a monster.

Sunny tries to explain that the Soul Tree is a trap, not a protector, and that they will become its slaves, but Nephis only says that he has lost his mind. She raises her sword and tells him to let Cassie go. He sets Cassie down, and before he finishes speaking, Nephis moves faster than he can follow and he is lying on the ground with the sword at his throat. He had thought he had a chance against her now, but he lasted a second. With the blade on his skin, he shouts, 'Aster, Song, Vale!'

Her hand trembles, drawing a drop of blood, and her eyes widen. She asks how he knows those names and who he is, and demands to know which Domain he belongs to. He says honestly that he did not know they were names, only that she told him to say them if she forgot what had to be done, and he asks what a domain is. Her expression turns maniacal for a moment, then she stumbles, and her usual calm returns. She has not remembered everything, but enough to listen, and she lowers the sword and helps him up. When he asks her to have Cassie summon her staff and bring her to the boat, she does so, though he does not ask how she persuaded her.

Sunny pushes the boat into the dark sea at the last light of dusk, and Cassie's gale fills the sail. He steers from the stern, and watches the Soul Tree shrink behind them, wishing he were strong enough to destroy it. At the Barrow, he left a candle burning in a stone alcove next to a tall pile of leaves, seaweed, and demon fat. When the candle burns down, the pile ignites into a huge bonfire, rousing the dark sea. He vows to become powerful enough never to be afraid again. In the boat, Cassie suddenly lifts her head toward him, with a dark expression that fades into doubt.

The carapace boat cuts across the black sea in total silence broken only by creaking bone and water against metal. Sunny steers west by the mark that the shadow of the Crimson Spire left in his mind, since there is no moon or star. Several times he feels huge shadows moving close beneath the hull, drawn by the sound, and he can only tremble and hope they turn away. Their small size may not be worth the hunger of the leviathans.

A few hours into the voyage, his mind begins to clear, and then he hears a ghostly sound of shattering glass in his head. The last fog lifts. He is free of the Soul Devourer's enthrallment. Free of the haze, he sees clearly how insane their situation is, balanced above an abyss on a thin layer of steel, but in this place the craziest choice is sometimes the best.

Cassie hands the staff to Nephis, crawls to him through the dark and hugs him, crying silently and thanking him. He awkwardly tells her they are even since she warned him, and she apologizes in a strange voice, and moves back to the middle of the boat.

Left alone with the oar, Sunny counts what he got from the island: a new weapon, at least a hundred shadow fragments, and two new Attributes, a better Spark of Divinity and the mysterious Blood Weave. He wonders who Weaver is, who the Unknown are, and why the Memory's rank and type were blank. He also realizes from Nephis's words that Cassie's armor is a tier-six Memory, from an Awakened Terror, one class above Mountain King, which brings him one step closer to understanding how Nephis got her True Name.

Sunny realizes that Nephis may have killed an Awakened Terror in her First Nightmare, which is more astonishing than his own tyrant. He is nearly sure that her Aspect is also Divine rank, which explains why she can both heal and destroy, and wonders at the odds of two Sleepers with Divine Aspects meeting, which he suspects is his [Fated] Attribute at work, and which could turn out to be a blessing or a calamity, since her True Name can also be read as Star of Ruin. He recalls the fear he felt facing her sword. He also notes that she called the Drop of Ichor a 'Lineage Memory' without hesitation, that she knew the names Aster, Song, and Vale, and that she asked about domains, all of which suggest she knows a great deal about the Spell that the public does not.

As the night draws to a close and the hope of dawn rises, their luck runs out. With no warning, the sea boils and giant tentacles wrap around the hull. The boat is jerked sideways and metal shrieks. Nephis, at the bow, cuts at one tentacle but another coils around her and drags her under without a sound, leaving her silver sword stuck in the flesh of the tentacle. The hull is crushed and Sunny is thrown into the freezing water.

He swims up through tentacles and sees, a few hundred meters away, a giant stone hand rising from the sea, palm open to the sky. He swims toward it, then stops and looks back at the floating wreckage. Cassie, in her attention-repelling tunic, may have a chance. A voice in his head says to flee, that she is a burden, that he will die. He grits his teeth and dives back down, answering, 'Because I want to!'

For once Sunny is not driven by fear and despair but by defiant indignation. He is tired of bending to the world and clinging to hope just to survive. He realizes that he has changed without noticing, and that how he lives now matters more than whether. He dives into black water, using only his shadow sense, with salt stinging his bite marks. The tentacles are dragging fragments of the boat toward a vast maw far below, and he dodges them. Without Blood Weave, he thinks, he would have suffocated long ago.

He finally spots a small shape struggling against a big one, and finds Cassie being pulled down by a smaller tentacle coiled around her torso, her movements weakening as she suffocates. He grabs the tentacle, summons the Midnight Shard, and cuts through it just below the coil with slow, braced strokes, and when the tsuba nears the wound, he changes his grip and pulls the blade down until the tentacle is severed. Cassie is barely conscious and does not realize who he is. He holds her against his chest and swims up, but with his lungs burning, the surface far above, and the monster alerted, a wall of tentacles closes around them.

Then the whole sea turns white. A blinding radiance fills the water as if a small sun had ignited below, and the tentacles writhe as if in agony and their barrier falls apart. Sunny swims up as fast as he can, ignoring the danger of the speed. At last his head breaks the surface, and they both gasp air. The light is gone, and the darkness is back, with the first light of dawn on the eastern horizon. He sees the stone hand and swims toward it, holding Cassie.

Sunny is at the end of his rope, having not slept for days, having endured the Blood Weave transformation, resisted the enthrallment, broken his finger, sailed through the dark, and fought in the abyss. He keeps swimming through the rough water to the giant hand, helps Cassie climb onto the stone palm, and collapses with her. The tentacles seem to be gone, perhaps scared away by the light. He moves them higher, to the base of the index finger. Cassie asks what happened and then where Neph is. He tries to stay silent, but his Flaw presses until tears run down his face, and he begins to say, 'She's… she's g…'

Then a pale hand grabs the rock at the base of the thumb, and Nephis pulls herself up onto the palm. The Starlight Legion Armor is shattered, and she is nearly dead, with half her right side missing, ribs and organs exposed, a thigh torn to the bone, her right arm hanging by a strip of skin, one eye destroyed, and her face flayed. She falls to her knees as her femur shatters. Then white flames ignite in her eyes, her mouth, and her wounds, and her blood turns into liquid fire. The fire reshapes her flesh, setting bones, restoring organs, and filling in missing parts. She tears off the dangling arm and presses it to the stump, and the halves fuse. Soon there is only unmarked skin showing through the gaps in the armor. She looks at them without recognition, then loses consciousness as dawn begins.

Nephis stays unconscious for two days. On the third day, she wakes, puzzled to see Sunny grinning at her. He tells her to look behind her, and she turns to see a tall grey wall of polished stone rising from the slope of the great crater. They have found the human castle. 

 END OF VOL 1
